title: Jäänhoito- ja latukoneiden huolto- ja korjauspalvelut 2027 (2030)
description: Oulun Tilapalvelut -liikelaitos pyytää tarjousta Jäänhoito- ja latukoneiden huolto- ja korjauspalveluista sopimuskaudelle 1.1.2027 - 31.12.2027. Mahdolliset optiokaudet vuosi kerrallaan ajanjaksolle 1.1.2028 - 31.12.2030. Tilaaja ilmoittaa optioiden luopumisesta 3kk ennen optiokauden alkamista, muutoin optiot tulevat käyttöön ja voimaan automaattisesti. Hankinnasta perustetaan puitejärjestely. Osa-alueen etusijajärjestys määräytyy vertailun kokonaispistemäärän perusteella. Eniten pisteitä saanut tarjoaja sijoittuu ensimmäiseksi. Huoltopalvelun osa-alueilla vertailuperusteena on hinta. Akuuttikorjauksen osa-alueilla vertailuperusteina ovat hinta 95 pistettä ja samaa laitemerkkiä koskevan huoltopalvelun tarjoaminen 5 pistettä. Palveluntuottajia valitaan enintään kaksi per osa-alue. Varsinainen palveluntuottaja ja varasijalle toinen. Mikäli hyväksyttäviä tarjouksia saadaan vain yksi, tilaaja voi perustaa puitejärjestelyn kyseiseen osa-alueeseen yhden toimittajan kanssa. Kaikkia osa-alueita (kaikki jäänhoitokonemerkit) ei tarvitse tarjota. Tuntihintojen ja pisteytyskriteerien tarjoaminen tapahtuu "hankinnat kohdan kriteerit" kohdassa. Huolto- ja tuntihinnat tarjotaan per laitemerkki erikseen. Lisäpisteitä saa, jos samaan merkkiin tarjotaan sekä huolto- että korjauspalvelua. Tällöin korjauspalvelun kohdalla tulee merkitä ”kyllä” tarjottu huoltopalvelua. Tarjottuun hinta on esitettävä arvonlisäverottomina (alv 0 %) nettohintoina, jotka sisältävät kaikki palvelun tuottamisesta aiheutuvat kustannukset mahdolliset kilometri, matka-, majoitus-, päiväraha-, ylityö- sekä toimitus-, laskutus- ja toimistokulut mukaan lukien. Matka-ajasta saa laskuttaa tarjouslomakkeella ilmoitettua tuntihintaa enintään yhdeltä henkilöltä. Matka-aika lasketaan lyhintä tavanomaista ajoreittiä pitkin Oulun kaupungin hallinnolliselta rajalta tai toimittajan Oulun kaupungin alueella sijaitsevasta vakituisesta toimipisteestä työkohteeseen ja takaisin. Erillisiä kilometri-, päiväraha-, majoitus- tai muita matkakuluja ei saa laskuttaa. Mikäli 1. sijoittunut ei pysty /on estynyt ottamasta työtä vastaan, tilaaja käyttää 2. sijoittunutta palveluntarjoajaa. Valittu palveluntuottaja ei voi ilman perusteltua syytä kieltäytyä vastaanottamasta työtilausta ja perustelut annetaan kirjallisesti esim. sähköpostin välityksellä. Huoltopalvelun ja ei-kiireellisen korjauksen vasteaika arkisin on 5 vrk. (työn vastaanotto ja sen aloitus). Akuuttikorjauspalvelun vasteaika arkisin ja viikonloppuisin on 1 vrk. (työn vastaanotto ja sen aloitus). Töitä saavat tilata ainoastaan tilaajan nimeämät yhteyshenkilöt (työnjohtajat), jotka määrittelee erikseen työtä tilatessaan, onko työ huolto- vai ei-kiireellistä tai akuuttikorjaustyötä. Huoltopalvelu suoritetaan merkkivalmistajan huolto-ohjelman mukaisesti ja tarjoajalla tulee olla käytössään merkkivalmistajan tarjoamat ja ylläpitämät diagnostiikkatyökalut tai valmistajan hyväksymät tai teknisesti vastaavat. Huollot toteutetaan pääsääntöisesti kauden ulkopuolella yleensä touko- syyskuun välisenä ajankohtana. Huolto tapahtuu tilaajan tarjoamissa tiloissa Oulun talousalueella (Kanta Oulu, Haukipudas, Kiiminki, Ylikiiminki ja Yli-Ii). Akuuttikorjauspalvelu tehdään tilaajan tilaamana ennalta arvaamattomien vikatilanteiden osalta. Korjaustyö on akuuttia, välitöntä ja välttämätöntä korjausta, johon tulee reagoida sopimuksen mukaisella kiireellisellä aikataululla. Korjaukset tehdään pääsääntöisesti koneiden käyttöpaikalla maastossa. Huolto- ja korjauspalvelussa hankittavien varaosien tulee olla uusia ja alkuperäislaatuisia. Materiaaleille ja varaosille on voimassa kiinteä kateprosentti, joka on 5%. Alkuperäiset varaosien ostolaskut tulee liittää tilaajalle toimitettavaan laskuun mukaan. Tilaajalla on oikeus tarpeen mukaan tilata erikseen yksittäisiä varaosia ja tarvikkeita palveluntuottajalta omaan kalustoon. Tilaaja voi poistaa / lisätä huolto- ja korjauspalvelun piiriin kuuluvaa kalustoa vuosittain. Tilaaja informoi muutoksista palveluntuottajaa. Mikäli Tilaajalle tulee uusia tarjouspyynnössä mainitsemattomia laitemerkkejä, voi tilaaja pyytää puitesopimuskumppaneilta minikilpailutuksen kautta tarjoushinnat uudelle laitemerkille. Tarjoukset eivät saa sisältää omia ehtoja. Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu mihinkään hankintamäärään. Tilaajalla on oikeus hylätä kaikki tarjoukset perustellusta syystä. Voor de werking van de raamovereenkomst en het plaatsen van nadere opdrachten wordt verwezen naar paragraaf H2.8. title: Flight System Team Systems Integration and Technical Expertise
description: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC) has a requirement for a four-month extension to contract 80MSFC24CA012 for engineering skills, manpower, and technical capability needed by the Flight Systems Team within the Human Exploration Development and Operation Chief Engineer�s Office within the Engineering Directorate. The tasks involved with this work cover all phases of ongoing vehicle systems integration and testing, as well as design support for future mission planning efforts. In addition, this contract also provides specialized technical engineering expertise, as well as ground and on-orbit test support, for proprietary flight platforms. The required support involves access to proprietary vehicle design information, interface documentation, and anomaly resolution data. Resolution, LLC personnel currently possess the necessary access, knowledge, and integration history to analyze and apply this information without interruption to ongoing operations. NASA MSFC intends to issue a sole source contract modification to acquire these services from Resolution, LLC for an additional four (4) months through April 30, 2027, under the authority of FAR 6.103-1, 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), �Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.� Pursuant 6.103-1, Resolution�s team serves in a Chief Engineer advisory capacity and provides critical technical oversight and independent engineering assessment throughout the platform lifecycle. NASA/MSFC has maintained a dedicated government-led team, consisting of both civil servants and contractor personnel, in continuous support of this program since 1999. With over more than two decades of support, the team has developed unique institutional knowledge, specialized analytical tools, and mission-specific expertise necessary to track and resolve vehicle anomalies; document design, test, and operational issues; capture and apply lessons learned; implement systems engineering best practices; monitor and assess flight performance data; support launch, ascent, on-orbit, recovery, and post-flight operations; and provide engineering recommendations to inform vehicle modifications, upgrades, and future mission planning. Resolution, LLC maintains a workforce with demonstrated experience supporting vehicle anomaly resolution, certification activities, interface verification, and operational engineering functions specific to the platform. The continuity of this highly specialized support is essential to maintaining mission effectiveness, preserving program knowledge, and ensuring the timely identification and resolution of technical issues affecting vehicle performance, reliability, and operational success. NASA/MSFC requires continued contract support under the current contract 80MSFC24CA012 beyond its current period of performance end date to continue providing systems engineering, integration, interface, verification, and certification support. The required support activities include Tracking and Data Relay Satellite System (TDRS) requirements decomposition, legacy TDRS compatibility assessment, interface closure, demonstration planning, and technical preparations necessary for the commercial Ka band demonstration and transition to operations. These activities must continue without interruption to meet mission schedules and transition milestones. This extension will allow for uninterrupted services while NASA/MSFC assesses the results of market research and utilizes that information to continue with an appropriate procurement strategy. This work is within the existing scope of Contract 80MSFC24CA012 and represents a continuation of ongoing systems engineering, integration, interface management, verification, and certification support currently being performed by Resolution, LLC. Failure to execute this continuation would result in unnecessary schedule impacts and increased technical, integration, and programmatic risk associated with transition and loss of critical knowledge. Accordingly, Resolution, LLC is the only responsible source capable of providing the required services within the necessary time frame and with acceptable risk to the Government. The Government does not intend to acquire a commercial item using FAR Part 12. Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort electronically via email to Cynthia Hubbard at Cynthia.a.hubbard@nasa.gov, alternate contact Annette.Hawkins@nasa.gov no later than 10:00 am CST on Monday, December 7, 2026. Such capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this acquisition on a competitive basis. A determination by the Government not to compete this acquisition on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at : https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurement-Ombuds-Comp-Advocate-Listing.pdf

title: USACE SPK DBB Construction - Calaveras Wastewater Treatment Plant Improvements - Copperopolis, CA
description: This Sources Sought Notice is being issued for market research purposes to determine the availability, capability, and interest of small business firms for a potential Government requirement. NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE; requests for the solicitation will go unanswered. No award will be made from this Notice. Responses will be used to determine potential acquisition strategies, understand current market capabilities, and to gain knowledge of potential sources. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Sacramento District (SPK) anticipates a potential requirement for Design-Bid-Build (DBB) construction services to conduct Copper Cove Wastewater Treatment Plant (CCWTP) Improvements in collaboration with the Calaveras County Water District (CCWD) in Calaveras County, California (CA). The project is anticipated to include installation of a new continuous backwash filtration system to replace an existing filter system; electrical improvements to include upgrading the existing PG&E service size to the main switchboard located in the Control Building, installing a new transformer, raceways, metering panel, new Motor Control Center (MCC), and associated wiring and components; interconnection with a pre-existing CCWD-installed suspended air floatation (SAF) filter pretreatment system; installation of a new continuous backwash filter system to include excavation, shoring, and backfill for a partially buried cast-in-place concrete tank with three (3) equipped filter cells (modules), air control panel, grating and handrailing over the filter cells and feed channel; inlet and outlet piping, valves, and connection to existing ultraviolet (UV) inlet piping; and power and control tie-ins. The project is also anticipated to include construction of a new masonry compressor building on a concrete slab foundation, housing a duplex air compressor with space for an additional unit, along with appurtenant equipment on the compressed air piping including a refrigerated air dryer, oil-water separator, and air filter; a new wet well and submersible pump station to include a new buried precast wet well with an adjacent valve vault housing a duplex submersible pump station, valves and appurtenances, piping, and power control conduits constructed adjacent to the new SAF to convey filter backwash waste flow to the SAF. Finally, the project is anticipated to include demolition and disposal of the existing adsorption clarifier and mixed media filter equipment, dewatering of sludge handling facility solids in three (3) containerized, polymer-assisted gravity sludge dewatering systems that will be positioned on a concrete pad with containment walls and drainage systems to capture drained water and return it to Pond 6 through three (3) quick coupler hose connection points (one (1) per bin), and all associated yard pipe modifications to connect the new components to the existing WWTP, generally buried in suitable native or engineered backfill at depths of approximately three (3) to ten (10) feet of cover. The potential requirement may result in a firm-fixed-price construction solicitation issued approximately December 2026. If solicited, the Government intends to award the anticipated requirement by approximately March 2027. The Government estimates that construction of the anticipated requirement can be completed within three-hundred-sixty-five (365) calendar days from Contractor receipt of the Notice to Proceed. Work may also be impacted by bird nesting season, which runs from 1 February through 31 August. If market conditions indicate the estimated period of performance may be unrealistic, Respondents are encouraged to provide specific information (such as known equipment lead times or other timeline concerns) for Government consideration when responding to this Sources Sought Notice. The Government currently estimates the target price range for the anticipated project may be between $5,000,000.00 and $10,000,000.00. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code identified for the anticipated requirement is 237110, Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction. The small business size standard for the NAICS, as established by the U.S. Small Business Administration, is $45,500,000.00 annual revenue. The Product or Service Code (PSC) for the anticipated requirement is Y1PD, Construction of Waste Treatment and Storage Facilities. If there is a reasonable expectation that two (2) or more responsible small business concerns under the NAICS can provide the anticipated services, the Contracting Officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. If competition is set-aside for competition limited to small businesses, Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting (Deviation), requires that construction small business Contractors self-perform at least twenty-five percent (25%) of the cost of the contract, excluding the cost of materials. If no set aside is made, the requirement is competed with full and open competition, and the awarded Contractor is not a small business, the Contractor may be required to self-perform a percentage of work if required in the solicitation. Contractors with the skill, capabilities, workload capacity, and ability to obtain bonding to complete the project described above (either through self-performance and/or Subcontractor management) are invited to provide capability statements to the primary point of contact listed below. Other than small businesses are also encouraged to submit Capability Statements. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Responses must be limited to ten (10) 8.5 x 11 inch pages with a minimum font size of point 10. Please provide the following information: 1) Company name, System for Award Management (SAM) Unique Entity Identification (UEID) number or Employer Identification Number (EIN), address, point of contact name, contact phone number, contact e-mail address, and statement identifying whether the company employs union or non-union workers. 2) Experience and capability to complete contracts of similar magnitude and complexity to the potential requirement, including at least three (3) examples of comparable work performed within the past six (6) years. Each example should include a brief description of the project, description of the work performed (identification of self-performance and/or Subcontractor management), customer name, customer satisfaction, timeliness of performance, dollar value of the project, and whether there were any challenges experienced during the project (delays, investigations, health and safety issues, labor shortages, management / organizational issues, etc.). 3) Business size and socioeconomic type for the applicable NAICS (ex: Woman-Owned Small Business, Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), certified Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), 8(a) Participant, small business, or other than small business (large business)). 4) Bonding capability (in the form of a Surety letter). Please submit all capabilities statements, information, brochures, and/or marketing material as one (1) document, limited to the page quantity above. Responses will not be considered an offer, proposal, or bid for any solicitation that may result from this Notice. Moreover, responses will not restrict the Government to an acquisition approach. This Notice is for information and planning purposes only. Respondents will not be notified of the results of any review conducted or the capability statements received. Please provide responses and/or questions by e-mail to the Contract Specialist, Costa Laliotitis, at (Constantinos.Laliotitis@usace.army.mil) by 0800 / 8:00 a.m. Pacific Time on Monday, 7 December 2026. Please include the Sources Sought Notice number W9123827X1CHG in the e-mail subject line.

title: Flight System Team Systems Integration and Technical Expertise
description: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC) has a requirement for engineering skills, manpower, and technical capability needed by the Flight Systems Team within the Human Exploration Development and Operation Chief Engineer�s Office within the Engineering Directorate. The tasks involved with this work cover all phases of ongoing vehicle systems integration and testing, as well as design support for future mission planning efforts. In addition, this contract also provides specialized technical engineering expertise, as well as ground and on-orbit test support, for proprietary flight platforms. The required support involves access to proprietary vehicle design information, interface documentation, and anomaly resolution data. Resolution, LLC personnel currently possess the necessary access, knowledge, and integration history to analyze and apply this information without interruption to ongoing operations. NASA MSFC intends to issue a sole source contract modification to acquire these services from Resolution, LLC. under the authority of FAR 6.103-1, 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), �Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.� Pursuant 6.103-1, Resolution�s team serves in a Chief Engineer advisory capacity and provides critical technical oversight and independent engineering assessment throughout the platform lifecycle. NASA/MSFC has maintained a dedicated government-led team, consisting of both civil servants and contractor personnel, in continuous support of this program since 1999. With over more than two decades of support, the team has developed unique institutional knowledge, specialized analytical tools, and mission-specific expertise necessary to track and resolve vehicle anomalies; document design, test, and operational issues; capture and apply lessons learned; implement systems engineering best practices; monitor and assess flight performance data; support launch, ascent, on-orbit, recovery, and post-flight operations; and provide engineering recommendations to inform vehicle modifications, upgrades, and future mission planning. Resolution, LLC maintains a workforce with demonstrated experience supporting vehicle anomaly resolution, certification activities, interface verification, and operational engineering functions specific to the platform. The continuity of this highly specialized support is essential to maintaining mission effectiveness, preserving program knowledge, and ensuring the timely identification and resolution of technical issues affecting vehicle performance, reliability, and operational success. NASA/MSFC requires continued contract support under the current contract 80MSFC24CA012 beyond its current period of performance end date to continue providing systems engineering, integration, interface, verification, and certification support. The required support activities include Tracking and Data Relay Satellite System (TDRS) requirements decomposition, legacy TDRS compatibility assessment, interface closure, demonstration planning, and technical preparations necessary for the commercial Ka band demonstration and transition to operations. These activities must continue without interruption to meet mission schedules and transition milestones. This extension will allow for uninterrupted services while NASA/MSFC assesses the results of market research and utilizes that information to continue with an appropriate procurement strategy. This work is within the existing scope of Contract 80MSFC24CA012 and represents a continuation of ongoing systems engineering, integration, interface management, verification, and certification support currently being performed by Resolution, LLC. Failure to execute this continuation would result in unnecessary schedule impacts and increased technical, integration, and programmatic risk associated with transition and loss of critical knowledge. Accordingly, Resolution, LLC is the only responsible source capable of providing the required services within the necessary time frame and with acceptable risk to the Government. The Government does not intend to acquire a commercial item using FAR Part 12. Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort electronically via email to Cynthia Hubbard at Cynthia.a.hubbard@nasa.gov, alternate contact Annette.Hawkins@nasa.gov no later than 10:00 am CST on Monday, December 7, 2026. Such capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this acquisition on a competitive basis. A determination by the Government not to compete this acquisition on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. USACE anticipates a requirement under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 541330, Engineering Services. The Government contemplates and unrestricted procurement with a reserve for Small Business concerns for a Firm Fixed Price Multiple Award Task Order Contracts (MATOC) for MVN Civil Works Program & Project Management Support Services. The requirement: USACE New Orleans District seeks responsive and responsible small business offerors who shall provide services for the Civil Works Program & Project Management Support Services for efforts related to the water resources programs in southern Louisiana including USACE Civil Works Programs. Services include project management/planning support, development of project performance reports, updates to program management plans, project scheduling input, project cost support, presentation development, interagency agreement development /updates, project drawings and maps, other project reports, and monthly status reports. Qualifications: The contractor shall have the capability of providing project management and planning support, development of project performance reports, updates to Project/Program Management Plans (PMPs), project scheduling analysis, project cost tracking support, development of project performance reports, project cost tracking support, development of briefings and presentations, interagency agreement support, mapping and spatial project visual support, and monthly contract status reports. The contractor shall formulate flood risk management, navigation, and ecosystem restoration plans supported by quantitative benefits analysis. The contractor shall conduct studies, inventory and forecast of problems and opportunities, formulation of measures and alternative plans, evaluation and comparison of alternatives plans, evaluation and comparison of alternatives, calculation and comparison of monetized and non-monetized benefits. The contractor shall prepare documents such as federal interest determination, reconnaissance, feasibility, post-authorization and other reports, including cultural resources studies and reports, and hazardous, toxic, and radiological waste (HTRW) investigations, National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and /or other environmental quality documents. The contractor shall document water and wastewater issues as necessary to develop master plan level documents for environmental infrastructure, PAS, SJ, CAP, and other programs as required. The contractor shall develop ecosystems habitat surveys, endangered or threatened species surveys, wetlands assessments using standard State of Louisiana methods in coopetition with other Federal and State agencies, modeling, and mitigation and monitoring plans. The contractor shall coordinate with Corps, non-Federal partners, and other stakeholders to document existing flood damage problems, historical flood maps, potential ecosystem restoration, and recreation problems and opportunities within the study area. The contractor shall coordinate with Corps and non-Federal partners to document required excavation permits, utility easements, rights-of-way, and other project-related requirements shortly after exercising this contract. The contractor shall document all or part of NEPA and/or other environmental documents, including, but not limited to, Biological and HTRW assessments, Environmental Assessments (EA), and Environmental Impact Statements (Els's). description: 1.0 DESCRIPTION THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation for bids, proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Enterprise Procurement Office (EPO), formerly the Strategic Acquisition Center (SAC), is issuing this Sources Sought Notice as a means of conducting market research to identify qualified sources with the capability and resources to meet the Veterans Health Administration s (VHA) Non-Expendable Equipment National Program requirement for Sterilizer Unit Low Temperature H2O2, with 3D printed items sterilization capabilities. The EPO in conjunction with VHA is seeking qualified sources capable of supplying the Steris Corporation® V-Pro Max 2 Sterilizer or equivalent products that satisfy the Salient Characteristics on an agency-wide basis. VA is contemplating the award of a single Requirements Contract with Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) orders IAW FAR 16.503, Requirements Contracts, to a supplier of this equipment. Respondents will be required to deliver complete Steris Corporation® V-Pro Max 2 Sterilizer to VA medical centers and facilities throughout the United States. The associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 339113 Surgical Appliance and Supplies Manufacturing and the associated size standard is 800 employees. The FAR Provision found at 52.204-7 requires that The Offeror shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer or quotation. You may access the SAM website at SAM.gov | Home. All respondents must be certified with the appropriate NAICS code on the SAM website. All Service Disable Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) / Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) respondents must be verified in the SBA database at: https://www.sba.gov/veterans/#vetcert at the time of submission. Submissions for this Sources Sought Notice shall be submitted by email no later than December 9, 2026, at 12:00pm Eastern Time to the Contract Specialist and Contracting Officer at the following email addresses: Joseph.Jeranek@va.gov Kimberly.LeMieux@va.gov Email responses shall include the following subject line: Response to Sources Sought Notice 36C10X27Q0031. This notice is part of a continuous process for obtaining the latest information on the commercial status of the industry with respect to their current and near-term abilities. The information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for, or award, a competitive contract. It is emphasized that this is a notice solely for planning and informational purposes. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. The Government may or may not issue a solicitation as a result of this notice. There is no solicitation available at this time. 2.0 SCOPE OF WORK The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Non-Expendable Equipment National Program has identified the Sterilizer Unit Low Temperature H2O2, with 3D printed items sterilization capabilities, as a candidate for a Veterans Affairs (VA)-wide (otherwise referred to as national ) single Requirements contract award. The Low Temperature, Gaseous Plasma, Vaporized Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2), Sterilizers are used for low temperature sterilization of heat and moisture-sensitive medical devices. Hydrogen peroxide is a known antimicrobial agent that oxidizes key cellular components within microorganisms, thereby destroying them. A low-temperature gaseous plasma sterilizer is an apparatus that uses vaporized hydrogen peroxide gas plasma to sterilize heat- and moisture-sensitive medical instruments and devices. The process involves injecting hydrogen peroxide vapor into a chamber, then applying an electrical field to create gas plasma. This plasma generates microbicidal free radicals that disrupt cellular components of microorganisms, killing them effectively. The process leaves behind harmless byproducts, water and oxygen, and is suitable for delicate equipment that cannot withstand high temperatures or humidity. Sterilization typically occurs at a temperature of less than 56°C with process times of around 25 to 70 minutes depending upon cycles type. title: Request for Information (RFI) Enhanced Maritime Biological Detection (EMBD) Identification Subsystem (IDS)
description: The Joint Product Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Sensing (JPdM CS), under the Joint Project Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Integrated Early Warning (JPM CBRN IEW), under the Portfolio Management Executive Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense (PME CBRND) within the Department of War (DoW), is conducting market research to identify potential industry sources capable of providing a Biological Warfare Agent (BWA) identification capability for integration into the U.S. Navy's Enhanced Maritime Biological Detection (EMBD) system. As a backward-compatible replacement for the Joint Biological Point Detection System (JBPDS) Identifier, the EMBD Identification Subsystem (IDS) automatically provides confirmatory identification of Biological Warfare Agents (BWAs) in liquid samples. In operation, the EMBD Collector gathers the sample externally and routes it to the IDS via the EMBD Fluid Transfer System (FTS). Please see the attached formal Request for Information (RFI) for full details.

title: NOTICE OF INTENT: DIRECT NEGOTIATED SALE OF SURPLUS FEDERAL VESSEL EX-VADM K.R. WHEELER (T-AG-5001) FOR OPERATIONAL COMMERCIAL RE-USE
description: UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION MARITIME ADMINISTRATION OFFICE OF SHIP DISPOSAL PROGRAMS (MAR-640) � WASHINGTON, D.C. 20590 NOTICE OF INTENT: DIRECT NEGOTIATED SALE OF SURPLUS FEDERAL VESSEL EX-VADM K.R. WHEELER (T-AG-5001) FOR OPERATIONAL COMMERCIAL RE-USE Notice Type Special Notice / Notice of Intent Primary Statutory Authority 46 U.S.C. � 57102; 40 U.S.C. � 545(b)(2) Proposed Disposition Action Direct Negotiated Commercial Re-Use Sale (Sales Contract MA-14564) Proposed Purchaser To Be Disclosed Upon Execution Pursuant to Statutory Requirements This is a notice of intent, not a request for a quotation or competitive proposal. A solicitation document will not be issued, and quotations, bids, or proposals will not be requested or accepted. 1. Statutory Authority and Action Summary The United States Department of Transportation, Maritime Administration (MARAD), acting by and through the Office of Ship Disposal Programs (MAR-640), pursuant to 46 U.S.C. � 57102 and 40 U.S.C. � 545(b)(2), hereby provides public notice of its intent to execute Sales Contract No. MA-14564 for the direct negotiated sale and transfer of title of the surplus National Defense Reserve Fleet (NDRF) vessel Ex-VADM K.R. WHEELER (T-AG-5001), IMO No. 9354038, for operational commercial re-use at a purchase price matching or exceeding the government's verified Fair Market Value appraisal. This disposition is conducted pursuant to MARAD�s primary maritime vessel disposal authorities under 46 U.S.C. � 57102 and the national security negotiated disposal exemption under 40 U.S.C. � 545(b)(2), independent of standard General Services Administration (GSA) competitive auction mechanisms. Conveyance of title and delivery shall occur strictly from MARAD custody at the Beaumont Reserve Fleet (Beaumont, TX) on an "AS IS, WHERE IS" basis. 2. Asset Identification and Condition Government Asset Designation Ex-VADM K.R. WHEELER (T-AG-5001) IMO / Registry Number IMO No. 9354038 Current Custody & Location Beaumont Reserve Fleet (Beaumont, TX) / Inactive NDRF Fleet Primary Technical Capabilities Offshore Petroleum Distribution System (OPDS) platform equipped with specialized dynamic positioning systems, deep-water fluid discharge apparatus, and high-volume pumping infrastructure. Conveyance Terms Conveyed strictly "AS IS, WHERE IS" with full buyer indemnification and mandatory post-closing hull biofouling and towing remediation obligations. Appraised Fair Market Value At or above verified Fair Market Value (established by formal appraisal from the Office of Shipyards & Marine Engineering). 3. Statutory Framework and Primary Considerations for Direct Negotiated Disposition Pursuant to 46 U.S.C. � 57102, 40 U.S.C. � 545(b)(2), and 41 CFR � 102-38.105(e), the Maritime Administration has determined that a direct negotiated sale of the Ex-VADM K.R. WHEELER for operational commercial re-use best serves national security, statutory directives, and the public interest based upon the following core determinations: Preservation of Critical National Security Infrastructure (OPDS): The Ex-VADM K.R. WHEELER was uniquely constructed as the primary operational platform for the Offshore Petroleum Distribution System (OPDS), capable of delivering bulk petroleum products to military forces in austere or degraded maritime environments. Commercial re-use and transfer into the U.S. Flag commercial fleet ensures the private-sector reactivation and maintenance of these specialized logistics systems, preserving strategic surge capability for U.S. Transportation Command (USTRANSCOM) and Military Sealift Command (MSC) at zero ongoing federal expense. Proprietary Technical and Engineering Data Compliance: Safe reactivation, United States Coast Guard (USCG) certification, and sustained commercial operation of the vessel require lawful access to specialized technical data, original build schematics, and proprietary dynamic positioning intellectual property. Direct negotiation ensures transfer to an entity demonstrating verified proprietary data rights and operational capacity to achieve Coast Guard compliance without government indemnification. Statutory and Regulatory Defense Covenants: The conveyance contract requires enforceable covenants running with the vessel, including U.S. documentation restrictions under 46 CFR Part 221, a statutory 10-year foreign trade restriction surety bond pursuant to 46 U.S.C. � 57102, and prohibitions against unauthorized foreign transfer, re-flagging, or premature scrapping. Elimination of Federal Liabilities and Fund Recovery: Direct disposition terminates ongoing layberth, hull maintenance, security, and environmental compliance overhead, while net proceeds are statutorily deposited into dedicated maritime accounts under 46 U.S.C. � 57103 to support NDRF operations and training programs. 4. Public Notice Information and Inquiries This posting is published for public transparency and statutory reporting awareness. As a non-competitive negotiated disposition under 40 U.S.C. � 545(b)(2) and 46 U.S.C. � 57102, no solicitation will be released and no bids, capability statements, or quotations are solicited. Ship Sales Contracting Officer Office of Acquisition (MAR-640) Program Office Office of Ship Disposal Programs (MAR-640) Point of Contact / Email nathaniel.williford@dot.gov Program Office Direct Line (202) 366-3653

title: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor Maintenance Dredging
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC) requires a contract to provide maintenance dredging for (3) dredging projects. The areas of consideration for these dredging services are: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor.Calcasieu River Bar Channel: Work for the Calcasieu River Bar Channel will require one fully crewed and equipped self-propelled trailing suction type hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -45ft MLLW and place dredged material into the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Sites (ODMDS).Pascagoula Harbor: Work for the Pascagoula Harbor maintenance dredging will require a hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -46 ft MLLW and place dredged material in the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Site (ODMDS). Dredged material shall be placed within Pascagoula ODMDS. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within 3-5 miles of the dredge cut.Panama City Harbor: Work for the Panama City Harbor maintenance dredging will require a medium to small hopper. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -40 ft MLLW and place dredged material within channel adjacent to the entrance jetty. Dredged material shall be placed within the channel adjacent to the jetty. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within one mile of the dredge cut. The following will be the performance periods:Calcasieu River Bar Channel: 15 January 2027 to TBDPascagoula Harbor: 01 April 2027 to 30 September 2027Panama City Harbor: 01 August 2027 to 30 September 2027This solicitation is unrestricted. The contract issued will be Firm Fixed Price. This solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be available on or about 23 October 2026. The bid opening date will be specified in the solicitation when it is issued. No additional media (CD-ROM, floppy disks, facsimiles, etc.) will be provided. title: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor Maintenance Dredging
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC) requires a contract to provide maintenance dredging for (3) dredging projects. The areas of consideration for these dredging services are: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor. Calcasieu River Bar Channel: Work for the Calcasieu River Bar Channel will require one fully crewed and equipped self-propelled trailing suction type hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -45ft MLLW and place dredged material into the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Sites (ODMDS).Pascagoula Harbor: Work for the Pascagoula Harbor maintenance dredging will require a hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -46 ft MLLW and place dredged material in the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Site (ODMDS). Dredged material shall be placed within Pascagoula ODMDS. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within 3-5 miles of the dredge cut. Panama City Harbor: Work for the Panama City Harbor maintenance dredging will require a medium to small hopper. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -40 ft MLLW and place dredged material within channel adjacent to the entrance jetty. Dredged material shall be placed within the channel adjacent to the jetty. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within one mile of the dredge cut. The Contractor shall commence dredging no later than 30 January 2027 in Calcasieu River Bar Channel. The order of work is as follows: (1) Calcasieu River Bar Channel, (2) Pascagoula Harbor, (3) Panama City Harbor. This solicitation is unrestricted. The contract issued will be Firm Fixed Price. This solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be available on or about 23 October 2026. The bid opening date will be specified in the solicitation when it is issued. No additional media (CD-ROM, floppy disks, facsimiles, etc.) will be provided. Paper copies of this solicitation will not be available. Other methods of requesting a package will not be honored. title: Department of War Pharmacy Uniform Formulary Blanket Purchase Agreement/Uniform Formulary Additional Discount Program
description: The Department of War (DoW) is required by law (10 U.S.C. � 1074g) to establish an effective, efficient, integrated pharmacy benefits program for the Military Health System (MHS) which includes the purchase pharmaceutical agents. The law and implementing regulation (32 CFR Section 199.21) describe the process by which the DoW Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) Committee will consider the relative clinical effectiveness and relative cost effectiveness of pharmaceutical agents in a therapeutic class in recommending the selection of agents for the DoW Uniform Formulary (UF) and, for cost sharing purposes, the classification of a pharmaceutical agent as generic, formulary, Basic Core Formulary (BCF), Extended Core Formulary (ECF), or non-formulary (NF). Prior to the scheduled P&T Committee meeting, a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for pharmaceutical agents within Drug Classes identified for placement on the UF has been issued to obtain quotes from industry. The Defense Health Agency may award Uniform Formulary Blanket Purchase Agreements (UF BPA) and the Uniform Formulary Additional Discount Program Agreements (UF ADP) based on the UF decision. This process is described in the attached RFQ. P&T COMMITTEE MEETING: The following February 2027 drug classes/subclasses will be reviewed: a. REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. title: 99 CS Commercial TV over IPTV
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12, following RFO 12.201-1 Simplified Procedures, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The Government reserves the right to award without discussions or to make no award at all depending upon (1) the quality of quotes received and (2) whether proposed prices are determined to be fair and reasonable.1. The solicitation number is FA486127Q0002. This solicitation is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP). A Firm Fixed Price type contract will be awarded.2. The incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01, effective 13 March 2026.3. This combined synopsis/solicitation is being issued as a Full and Open Competition, and the associated NAICS code is 517111 - Wired Telecommunications.4. DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES: The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform installation, maintenance, and delivery of High-Definition (HD) local and cable television programming to designated areas of the facility. Service must be fully compatible with the Governments existing hardware, specifically the Haivision Play 2000-C Set-Top Box, for use with the Haivision IPTV Media Platform or as a stand-alone solution. This Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) establishes an enterprise-wide commercial television solution for Nellis Air Force Base. It encompasses the following cost components:Line of Effort (LOE) 1 (Core Headend Feed): A central IPTV multi-channel feed delivered directly to Government-Furnished Equipment (GFE) Haivision Encoders, managed by the 99th Communications Squadron. Line of Effort (LOE) 2 (Decentralized Endpoint Services): Monthly fee per active television connection, to be utilized by the 99 ABW Command Post and other authorized tenant units via separately funded Call Orders. Premium Channels: Monthly subscriptions for additional premium programming channels, as requested by authorized units.Initial Setup / Stream Configuration: A one-time activation, installation, and programming configuration charge (if applicable).Pricing Instruction: Offerors shall submit their pricing using Attachment 2 - Price List (Fillable PDF). Offerors must input their proposed monthly costs for LOE 1, LOE 2, and Premium Channels, and their one-time cost for Initial Setup. The quantities are locked at 12 months (for recurring items) and 1 each (for one-time items) to establish a standardized 12-month Total Evaluated Price (TEP) baseline for evaluation. Offerors shall not alter the locked quantities or pre-programmed formulas in Attachment 2 - Price List.

description: THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY AND DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION. THE SUBMISSION OF PRICING, CAPABILITIES FOR PLANNING PURPOSES, AND OTHER MARKET INFORMATION IS HIGHLY ENCOURAGED AND ALLOWED UNDER THIS RFI IN ACCORDANCE WITH (IAW) FAR 15.201(e). DISCLAIMER This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly. IAW RFO 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. SOURCES SOUGHT DESCRIPTION This is NOT a solicitation announcement. This is a sources sought/RFI only. The purpose of this sources sought/RFI is to gain knowledge of potential qualified sources and their size classification relative to NAICS 513210 (size standard of $47 Million). Responses to this sources sought will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. After review of the responses to this sources sought, a solicitation announcement may be published. Responses to this sources sought synopsis are not considered adequate responses for a solicitation announcement. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), HSA 5.3 Network Contracting Office, is seeking sources that can provide an Electronic Quality Management Software System that at a minimum meets the attached Statement of Work with a brand name or equal. Electronic Quality Management Software System STATEMENT OF WORK Scope The desired service is required for an electronic Quality Management web-based software platform for quality management of HSA 5.3 Pathology & Laboratory Medicine Service (PLMS). Modules requested are: Document Control Competency Assessment Non-Conforming Event Management Training Program Inspection Preparedness tools capable of supporting checklist management through methods permitted by each accreditation agency s licensing agreements. CAP checklists may only be used in accordance with CAP intellectual property policies. Services to be provided include complete software set up and configuration, conversion from previous formats, onsite or web-based training, software upgrades, and ongoing client support. QMS Software Requirements. Access The software must provide unlimited (24/7/365) access for approximately 700 -1000 unique user profiles. Software allows for multiple users to be assigned to different permissions/roles as needed by facility. Users can be assigned multiple permissions and roles within software. Operational Features Must include software upgrades for new versions of the software including updates to the current version. Software must be compatible with the VA available browser that VHA subscribes to (currently Chrome version 142.x, Or Microsoft Edge version 142.x) Additional supporting software or plug-ins that are required to be installed (including new versions) on VA owned hardware in order to operate the system properly must be on the VA Technology/Standard List. 99% annual operational uptime of system. Backup solution including an off-site, live fail-over server which can be activated within a short time in case of catastrophic failure. Data must be exportable in non proprietary formats (e.g., CSV, XML, PDF) to meet VA Records Management requirements in the event the company ceases operations or at the completion of the contracted time. Technical Features Solution must be a commercially off the shelf product that is available for full installation within 30 days of the award. Solution must be FedRAMP Moderate (or higher) authorized and must obtain and maintain a VA Authority to Operate (ATO) prior to production use. The software must have the ability to allow access to multiple users at multiple sites simultaneously. Must be web based. Ability to connect into our active directory for log in and email functions. System must be compatible with a PIV (Personal Identity Verification) card, 2 factor authentication login system. If solution offered is deemed to be SaaS, vendor complies with all VA security requirements for hosting documents as specified containing User Identifiable, business critical information. Have workflows and documents organized and managed by division/site; available across enterprise (all sites within V22 PLMS). The system must be compliant with all Office of Information and Technology and Information Security directives. The contractor s performance must be in compliance with all applicable state, federal and local laws and regulations. If the product is to be installed on VA equipment on the VA system, the solution/product supplied by the contractor must be approved in the VA Technical Reference Model (TRM) prior to use or installation. https://www.oit.va.gov/Services/TRM/TRMHomePage.aspx. If the contractor provides direct remote support within the VA system, the contractor must obtain a VA Interconnection Security Agreement (ISA) and complete all required VA security documentation (e.g., SSP, PTA/PIA) in support of ATO without impacting installation timeframes in section 5 Upgrade/Updates The Contractor shall provide updates to both the equipment hardware and software in order to maintain the integrity of the system and the state-of the art technology, at no additional charge to the Government. These shall be provided as they become commercially available and at the same time as they are being provided to commercial customers. This requirement only applies to system updates that enhance the model of equipment being offered, i.e. new version of software, correction of software defect, update offered to commercial customers at no additional charge, upgrade to replace model of equipment no longer Contractor supported, etc. This does not refer to replacing the original piece of equipment provided under the IDIQ; however, it does refer to significant changes in the hardware operational capability. title: 99 CS Commercial TV over IPTV
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12, following RFO 12.201-1 Simplified Procedures, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The Government reserves the right to award without discussions or to make no award at all depending upon (1) the quality of quotes received and (2) whether proposed prices are determined to be fair and reasonable.1. The solicitation number is FA486127Q0002. This solicitation is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP). A Firm Fixed Price type contract will be awarded.2. The incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01, effective 13 March 2026.3. This combined synopsis/solicitation is being issued as a Full and Open Competition, and the associated NAICS code is 517111 - Wired Telecommunications.4. DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES: The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform installation, maintenance, and delivery of High-Definition (HD) local and cable television programming to designated areas of the facility. Service must be fully compatible with the Governments existing hardware, specifically the Haivision Play 2000-C Set-Top Box, for use with the Haivision IPTV Media Platform or as a stand-alone solution. This Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) establishes an enterprise-wide commercial television solution for Nellis Air Force Base. It encompasses the following cost components:Line of Effort (LOE) 1 (Core Headend Feed): A central IPTV multi-channel feed delivered directly to Government-Furnished Equipment (GFE) Haivision Encoders, managed by the 99th Communications Squadron. Line of Effort (LOE) 2 (Decentralized Endpoint Services): Monthly fee per active television connection, to be utilized by the 99 ABW Command Post and other authorized tenant units via separately funded Call Orders. Premium Channels: Monthly subscriptions for additional premium programming channels, as requested by authorized units.Initial Setup / Stream Configuration: A one-time activation, installation, and programming configuration charge (if applicable).Pricing Instruction: Offerors shall submit their pricing using Attachment 2 - Price List (Fillable PDF). Offerors must input their proposed monthly costs for LOE 1, LOE 2, and Premium Channels, and their one-time cost for Initial Setup. The quantities are locked at 12 months (for recurring items) and 1 each (for one-time items) to establish a standardized 12-month Total Evaluated Price (TEP) baseline for evaluation. Offerors shall not alter the locked quantities or pre-programmed formulas in Attachment 2 - Price List. Submit offers via email to riley.finn@us.af.mil

title: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor Maintenance Dredging
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC) requires a contract to provide maintenance dredging for (3) dredging projects. The areas of consideration for these dredging services are: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor.Calcasieu River Bar Channel: Work for the Calcasieu River Bar Channel will require one fully crewed and equipped self-propelled trailing suction type hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -45ft MLLW and place dredged material into the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Sites (ODMDS).Pascagoula Harbor: Work for the Pascagoula Harbor maintenance dredging will require a hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -46 ft MLLW and place dredged material in the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Site (ODMDS). Dredged material shall be placed within Pascagoula ODMDS. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within 3-5 miles of the dredge cut.Panama City Harbor: Work for the Panama City Harbor maintenance dredging will require a medium to small hopper. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -40 ft MLLW and place dredged material within channel adjacent to the entrance jetty. Dredged material shall be placed within the channel adjacent to the jetty. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within one mile of the dredge cut. The following will be the performance periods:Calcasieu River Bar Channel: 15 January 2027 to TBDPascagoula Harbor: 01 April 2027 to 30 September 2027Panama City Harbor: 01 August 2027 to 30 September 2027This solicitation is unrestricted. The contract issued will be Firm Fixed Price. This solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be available on or about 23 October 2026. The bid opening date will be specified in the solicitation when it is issued. No additional media (CD-ROM, floppy disks, facsimiles, etc.) will be provided. Paper copies of this solicitation will not be available. Other methods of requesting a package will not be honored. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the size standard is $37,000,000.00. Offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) in order to be eligible to receive an award from any Government solicitation. Call 1-866-606-8220 for more information or visit the SAM website at www.sam.gov. After completing SAM, in order to download documents contractors and their subcontractors must register at www.sam.gov. In order to locate solicitation, Contractors can go to www. sam.gov and search for the solicitation number.Contractors can register to be put on a plan holders list that others can access through the www.sam.gov website. It is the Offerors responsibility to check the Internet address provided as necessary for any posted changes to this solicitation and all amendments. For additional information or assistance, please contact Cori Caimi, Contract Specialist, email cori.a.caimi@usace.army.mil or Rosalind Shoemaker, Contracting Officer, phone (910) 251-4436, email rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil.

description: Project Title: Department Of Energy - National Nuclear Security Administration Joint Cyber Facility Project Location: Building 810, Denver Federal Center, Lakewood, Colorado 80225 NAICS: 236220, Commercial & Institutional Building Construction Estimated Price Range: Between $10 and $20 million 1. Project Summary: The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), intends to procure construction services for a design-bid-build project for the development of a Joint Cyber Facility (JCF) for the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) at the Denver Federal Center in Lakewood, Colorado. This requirement for a new turnkey JCF consists of approximately 23,688 square feet of combined office and support space, including approximately 16,000 square feet of finished office workspace and 7,688 square feet of existing mechanical and electrical rooms supporting the space. The project includes integration of existing equipment from a prior data center installation. The finished space includes a reception area, offices, conference rooms, hoteling cubicles, pantry, server room, and a large video conferencing room. Construction and tenant build-out will occur within an occupied facility, necessitating careful coordination with active surrounding tenants. Work includes, demolition, architectural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, telecommunications, audio visual system infrastructure, security infrastructure, equipment, and coordinating installation of system furniture components, all of which must strictly adhere to accreditation requirements and standards. 2. title: Sources Sought Synopsis: Repair of NSN: 5840-01-659-4499
description: Notice Type: Sources Sought Synopsis 1. Notice This is not a solicitation, but rather a Sources Sought Synopsis to determine potential sources. This request is for information and planning purposes only. The purpose of this Sources Sought Synopsis is to conduct market research to determine if responsible sources exist; to assist in determining if this effort can be competitive, and/or a total Small Business Set-Aside. The proposed North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) Code is 811210, which has a corresponding Size standard of $34M in average annual receipts. The Government will use this information to determine the best acquisition strategy for this procurement. The Government is interested in all small businesses to include 8(a) Small Business Development Programs, Service-Disabled Veteran- Owned, Historically Under-utilized Business Zone(s) (HUBZone), and Women-Owned small business concerns. The Government requests that interested parties respond to this notice and identify your small business status relative to the identified NAICS code above. Additionally, please provide any anticipated teaming arrangements, along with a description of similar services offered to the Government and to commercial customers for the past three years. Any responses involving teaming agreements should delineate between the work that will be accomplished by the prime, and the work accomplished by the teaming partners. 2. Description Requirement Name: Repair of NSN: 5840-01-659-4499 For the end item, the contractor shall furnish all facilities, parts, materials, equipment and services required to inspect and, if necessary, restore to serviceable condition. The Government does not own the data or the rights to the software/data needed to purchase/repair this part through additional sources. It has been determined to be uneconomical to buy the data or rights to the data. It is uneconomical to reverse engineer the part. Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM): APPLIED SYSTEMS ENGINEERING INC CAGE: 3Z966 ADDRESS: 7510 Benbrook PKWY Benbrook, Texas 76126-2112, United States 3. Statement: Authority: 10 U.S.C. 2304(C)(1), Justification: Supplies required are available from only one or a limited number of responsible sources and no other type of supplies will satisfy agency requirements. This part requires engineering source approval by the design control activity in order to maintain the quality of the part. Existing unique engineering skills, and repair knowledge by the qualified source(s) require repair of the part by the approved source(s). The approved source(s) retain repair knowledge, or technical data that are not economically available to the Government, and the data or knowledge is essential to maintaining the quality of the part. An alternate source must qualify IAW the design control activity's procedures, as approved by the cognizant Government engineering activity. The qualification procedures must be approved by the Government engineering activity having jurisdiction over the part in the intended application. The Government does not own the technical data to provide contractors for qualification. 4. Anticipated Procurement Details Contract Type: Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) Period of Performance: 320 Days ARO 5. Capability Statement Submission Requirements Interested parties possessing the requisite capabilities are invited to submit a Capability Statement addressing the criteria outlined below. Business Information: Provide the following business information for your company: Company Name Address Point of Contact CAGE Code Phone Number E-mail Address Web Page Address Specify whether your company is a U.S. or foreign-owned firm Recommended North American Industry Classification System (NAICS Code) if other than 811210 Based on the above NAICS code, state whether your company is a small business and provide additional information regarding the type of small business (women-owned, small- disadvantaged, HUB Zone, etc.). Potential Offeror Capabilities: What is your experience in providing the capability to accomplish the objective/requirements listed above? Include contract numbers, a brief description of the work performed, period of performance, agency/organization supported, and individual points of contact (Contracting Officers or Program Managers). Provide pricing data, to include historical pricing data if available. How would the prime contractor account for government furnished property (GFP) in the possession of the prime, and all sub-contractors? Does your company currently have any teaming agreements in place that will allow for successfully meeting the Government's requirements? In addition, please identify the roles associated with the teaming arrangement. Discuss any documents or data you will require to complete the objectives listed above, and briefly explain their purpose. What are the top five risks you see in accomplishing this effort? How long would it take you to submit a proposal? Provide other relevant topics, concerns, or information not addressed in this posting. 6. Response Procedures Submission Format: Electronic format only (PDF preferred) Page Limit: Submissions must not exceed five (5) pages Due Date & Time: In accordance with (IAW) the date published on SAM.GOV Delivery Method: Submit via email to the points of contact on SAM.GOV 7. Disclaimer This is a Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS) issued in accordance with FAR Part 10 (Market Research) and FAR 15 (Contracting by Negotiation). This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or Invitation for Bid (IFB). Nothing in this document shall be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice, nor will it reimburse any costs incurred by interested parties in preparing or submitting responses. All information received in response to this notice marked "Proprietary" will be handled accordingly. The Government reserves the right to use non-proprietary information provided in market research reports, acquisition strategy determinations, and procurement development.

title: CAAA Rapid Acquisition Sustainment Program (RASP) BOA
description: AMENDMENT 0001 - PLEASE READ CAREFULLY! The purpose of this amendment is to formally update the solicitation and extend the proposal submission deadline as detailed below: 1. Change Set-Aside Status: This requirement is hereby converted from a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside to Full and Open Compeition (Unrestricted). Offers from all responsible commercial sources (large and small) will be considered. 2. Extended Closing Date: The proposal submission deadline is extended from 26 October 2026 to 07 December 2026 at 1:00pm CST. 3. Restructured CLINs: The solicitation is updated from 7 CLINs to 10 CLINs to align one-to-one with the 10 Categories in the Purchase Description 4. NAICS Code Registration Instruction: Added explicit guidance requiring offerors to hold the associated NAICS code in SAM.gov for any Category they wish to qualify for (see updated Section L, Paragraph 4). 5. Subcontracting Clauses Added: Incorporated FAR 52.219-8 (Utilization of Small Business Concerns) and FAR 52.219-9 (Small Business Subcontracting Plan). All updated attachments (Purchase Description, Attachment 0004) are uploaded below. Offerors must submit their revised proposals in accordance with these updated terms. SECTION A � SOLICITATION EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 1. THREE-STEP PROCUREMENT FRAMEWORK The Government will procure the Rapid Acquisition Sustainment Program (RASP) supply requirements utilizing a three-step process: Step One (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation): A separate Pre-solicitation Notice will not be issued; this synopsis is combined with the solicitation on SAM.gov in accordance with FAR Subpart 12.6. Individual order-level Request for Quotes (RFQs) under this Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) will be competed exclusively within the qualified pool and will not be synopsized, ensuring rapid execution. Clauses are in effect through FAC 2026-01. The primary NAICS code is 332710 (Machine Shops; Size Standard: 500 employees). Other codes are listed in Attachment 0001 - RASP BOA Purchase Description, and the Product Service Code is 5340 (Hardware, Commercial). Step Two (Master BOA Execution): The BOA Request for Proposal (RFP) will be released once for qualifications. The Government will execute no-cost, multi-award BOAs to responsible offerors whose proposals are compliant with Section L and rated "Acceptable" under Section M. BOAs are valid for up to five (5) years. NOTE: This RFP is the only opportunity to obtain a RASP BOA. Proposals will not be accepted or executed at any other time. If a contractor wishes to participate in any future RASP orders, they must respond to this initial RFP. Step Three (Order-Level Competition): As recurring supply needs arise, the PCO will issue competitive, order-level RFQs to the BOA pool. To participate, contractors must hold an active master BOA as of the RFQ closing date. Orders will result in individual, competitive Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contracts (Orders) under FAR 16.703. 2. SCOPE Contractors will provide commercial products supporting Crane Army Ammunition Activity (CAAA) operations across the categories defined in Section B. Items ordered may include detailed specifications from controlled technical data packages referencing military specifications (MIL-SPEC) or restricted technical drawings. 3. SUBCONTRACTING FLEXIBILITY Offerors must demonstrate technical capability within the scope of Attachment 0001- RASP BOA Purchase Description. Capability may be achieved with or without subcontractors. In Step Three order-level proposals, contractors are not bound to the subcontractors proposed in Step Two but must propose resources necessary to perform each individual order. 4. BASIS FOR AGREEMENT EXECUTION The Government will execute no-cost, multi-award BOAs to responsible offerors with compliant proposals (Section L) rated "Acceptable" (Section M). NOTE: The Government reserves the right to waive the Compliance Review if in its best interest. The Government intends to execute BOAs on initial proposals without discussions. It reserves the right to negotiate if in its best interest but will only do so with offerors whose proposals do not contain significant informational deficiencies. LEGAL NOTICE: This master BOA process is not a competitive acquisition; the source selection procedures of FAR Part 15 do not apply. No pricing is requested or evaluated at this stage. Execution of a BOA does not constitute a contract or guarantee future orders. SECTION B � CONTRACT LINE ITEM NUMBERS (CLINS) The following unfunded CLINs are established at the master agreement level for administrative categorization only: CLIN 0001: Machined and Fabricated Metal Parts (NAICS 332710 / 332999) CLIN 0002: Plastics and Injection Molded Components (NAICS 326199) CLIN 0003: Wooden Containers and Pallet Manufacturing (NAICS 321920) CLIN 0004: Ammunition and Nuclear Ordnance Boxes, Packages and Special Containers (NAICS 332439, 321920) CLIN 0005: Corrugated Fiberboard (Made and fabricated to specific dimensions) (NAICS 322211) CLIN 0006: Miscellaneous Fabricated Nonmetallic Materials (NAICS 326199) CLIN 0007: Chemicals (NAICS 325199, 325180) CLIN 0008: Paints and Coatings (NAICS 325510) CLIN 0009: Miscellaneous Hardware & Tools (NAICS 339991, 314994, 327910, 332510, 332613) CLIN 0010: Other Class IX Sustainment Products and Supplies (NAICS 423710) SECTION C � CAAA RASP EXECUTION BUSINESS RULES 1. GENERAL RULES A BOA is not a contract (FAR 16.703(a)). An order becomes a binding contract upon Government acceptance and award. The ordering period shall not exceed five (5) years from initial execution (DFARS 216.703(c)). Each BOA will be formally reviewed by the PCO annually (FAR 16.703(c)(2)) and revised as necessary. BOAs shall be changed only by modifying the agreement itself, not by individual orders. Modifications do not apply retroactively to active orders. Prior to the annual review, the PCO will confirm in writing if the contractor wishes to maintain the agreement. Either party may elect not to renew. The Government may cancel the BOA at any time if in its best interest. Only the Army Contracting Command�Rock Island Arsenal (ACC-RIA) is authorized to execute, modify, or perform annual reviews of these master BOAs. Other DoD activities may place orders under these BOAs with ACC-RIA approval. 2. STEP TWO EXECUTED BOAS (QUALIFICATION PHASE) Offerors must demonstrate technical capability in at least one (1) supply category listed in Attachment 0001- RASP BOA Purchase Description by completing Attachment 0004 � Combined Technical and Past Performance Questionnaire. No site visits are required at this stage. ***Offerors must possess an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) at the time of proposal submission. To be deemed administratively qualified for any given Category (Categories 1-10) under this solicitation, the offeror�s active SAM.gov profile must list the specific NAICS code(s) associated with that Category. For Categories that list multiple applicable NAICS codes, the offeror is only required to hold at least one (1) of the designated NAICS codes in their SAM.gov profile to be eligible for evaluation and award under that specific Category. Failure to hold the required NAICS code(s) in SAM.gov at the time of proposal submission will result in the immediate disqualification of the offeror�s proposal for that specific Category. 3. STEP THREE ORDER REQUESTS (ORDERING PHASE) Order competitions are limited to active master BOA holders. Order performance periods will be established in each order and remain valid through completion, even if they extend beyond the master BOA's 5-year term. Specific evaluation criteria (e.g., Price-Only, LPTA, or Tradeoff) will be identified in each order RFQ. Detail PDs, TDPs, and QA requirements will be provided at the order level. description: AMENDMENT 0001 - Extends Offer Due Date to December 7th, 2026 @1300 Central Time The Tonto National Forest is looking to achieve a more sustainable recreation program. Through this project, several recreation areas will be decommissioned in the Tonto Basin Ranger District (RD), and Globe RD. The decommission of campgrounds at the Tonto Bassin RD is the base bid and at Globe RD, it is an option bid. The intent of this work is to remove and safely dispose outside of the National Forest boundaries, recreational accommodations that include but not limited to Entry station buildings, toilets buildings, sidewalks, asphalt pavement, fish cleaning stations, septic system, and parking lots.
