title: Demolition of an existing building, Site Improvements and construction of a Modular Office Building at the US Merchant Marine Academy Campus, Kings Point, NY
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New York District intends to issue an invitation for bid to award a construction contract for the design and construction of a modular office space located along Steamboat Road on the US Merchant Marine Academy Campus (USMMA) adjacent to 307 Steamboat Road. The project magnitude is between $1-5M.This project will be advertised as 100% total Small Business Set-Aside. Summary of Work: The project objective is to design and provide a turnkey modular office facility. The scope includes the design and construction of a new office space of approximately 5,700 square feet, composed of custom modular units. The facility will be a single-story complex with a u-shaped space opening onto a small deck. It will house open offices with cubicles, six private offices, two conference rooms, four single-user bathrooms, a kitchenette/pantry room, lactation room, storage closets, and a mechanical room. The project scope encompasses incidental demolition, site prep work, foundations, underground utility hook ups, and site lighting. The contractor will also be responsible for providing furniture, fixtures, and equipment based upon the drawings and documentation provided in the Specifications package. The building and site infrastructure are required to have a minimum life expectancy of 10 to 15 years. The contract duration will be 136 calendar days for the entire project with phasing work involved. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is for general construction; 236220 for Commercial a nd Institutional Facilities. Solicitation has been posted. See link below. https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/74ce082cc2f34be4926ac48ccf9cf9a5/view

title: Pre-Clinical Models of Infectious Diseases
description: Pre-solicitation Notice Information Introduction The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), National Institutes of Health (NIH), of the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) supports research related to the basic understanding of microbiology and immunology leading to the development of vaccines, therapeutics, and medical diagnostics for the prevention, treatment, and diagnosis of infectious and immune-mediated diseases. The NIAID, Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases has a requirement to provide and develop animal models in order to advance our understanding of infectious diseases as well as advance the development of therapeutics and vaccines for infectious diseases. Description The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) supports and facilitates research that focuses on understanding, treating and, ultimately, preventing infectious, immunologic, and allergenic diseases. The NIAID Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (DMID) supports and facilitates research to understand, control and prevent human disease caused by infectious agents. Basic, applied and translational research to develop and assess therapeutics, vaccines, and diagnostics is supported through research grants, cooperative agreements, and contracts. In turn, DMID further supports and facilitates research ongoing under these funding mechanisms and through other programs via an array of preclinical and clinical resources and services to support multiples stages of the product development pipeline. These resources and services include genomic and gene sequencing services, provision of high quality biological materials, biocontainment facilities, and pre-clinical and clinical translational research resources (https://www.niaid.nih.gov/research/resources). The current NIAID Preclinical Models of Infectious Diseases IDIQ contract program is one of DMID�s preclinical services resources and supports the development and refinement of animal models and animal replacement models of infectious diseases, models that subsequently are used to evaluate candidate medical countermeasures against these diseases. In addition, these contracts facilitate regulatory submissions, patents, and other intellectual property applications by extramural investigators who request evaluation of their products. This program serves the DMID mission of supporting investigator-initiated research by providing critical data needed to apply for grant or other funding. Finally, these contracts enable product developers and sponsors to make key go/no-go decisions for candidate therapeutics, vaccines, and diagnostics. In addition to meeting the needs of extramural researchers, this program provides crucial data to our DHHS agency partners. These data will facilitate the advancement of promising candidate medical countermeasures against priority biodefense and emerging infectious agents to approval or licensure, and, in some cases, eventual deposit in the Strategic National Stockpile. As background, in 2024, 40 institutions were awarded base contracts under the Preclinical Models of Infectious Diseases IDIQ contract program. This program was a re-competition of her Animal Models of Infectious Diseases IDIQ contract program, and its overarching goal was to provide capability in a broad range of animal and animal replacement models for use in evaluating promising candidate countermeasures (vaccines, therapeutics, diagnostics) against the broad range of infectious agents that are in the purview of DMID. The breadth of the existing contractor pool has enabled a rapid and effective response to emerging infectious diseases, such as COVID-19, and emergency preparedness priorities. Awarded contracts were divided into 4 model-specific pools: Task Area A � Small Animal Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area B � Non-Human Primate Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area C � Animal Replacement and Non-traditional Animal Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area D � Generation and Distribution of Specialized Reagents The Preclinical Models of Infectious Diseases program will continue to provide the capability and capacity to develop and employ animal and animal replacement models (e.g., organ-on-a-chip technology) of infectious diseases for screening and product evaluation and addresses a critical stage in this pipeline by bridging in vitro testing and eventual clinical evaluation, including as needed, studies conducted under the guidance of 21 CFR 58, �Good Laboratory Practices�. In addition, for candidate products that are unable to be assessed for clinical efficacy in phase II or III trials for ethical or practical reasons, contracts awarded under this solicitation will enable regulatory approval or licensure via the guidance of the FDA�s Animal Efficacy Rule (21 CFR 314.610 and 601.91). This anticipated �ramp-on� solicitation will award multiple IDIQ base contracts to successful offerors that propose a general approach to the requirements, allowing them to join the existing contractor pools. Successful offerors will qualify for the pool and be eligible to compete for future task order awards in the existing model-specific Task Areas: Task Area A � Small Animal Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area B � Non-Human Primate Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area C � Animal Replacement and Non-traditional Animal Models of Infectious Diseases Task Area D � Generation and Distribution of Specialized Reagents Offerors are encouraged to consider submission of proposals to one or more of the above Task Areas (depending upon capabilities). Contract awards are anticipated to the organizations whose proposals offer the best value to the Government. For the purposes of this solicitation, the following definitions apply: Animal replacement tissue technologies derived from human or animal tissue (in particular lung, liver, immune system, brain, skin/soft tissue or gastrointestinal tissues): Organoids Organs on chips Artificial complex cell systems Microphysiological systems Tissue technologies derived from animals, in particular, non-human primates (for the purposes of bridging data from in vivo models with clinical data) Evaluation: encompasses advanced testing after a product has been screened and demonstrated as efficacious in the same or lower animal models; activities include dose refinement, measurement of host response, pharmacokinetics (in infected animals), pharmacodynamics (in infected animals), and therapeutic efficacy or immune protection against challenge. Model development: a novel systematic effort to reproduce a clinical syndrome caused by an infectious agent in an animal species following challenge with the agent and includes median lethal and/or infectious dose determination, natural history of infection, and serial pathogenesis studies. Model refinement: a systematic effort to improve the performance of an existing animal model that reproduces a clinical syndrome caused by an infectious agent; to adapt an existing animal model that reproduces a clinical syndrome caused by one infectious agent to a different, but related, infectious agent; to adapt an existing animal model to optimize its ability to support product screening or evaluation following challenge with the infectious agent. Non-human primate models: new and old-world species, including but not limited to Macaca, spp. (cynomolgus, Rhesus, pig-tailed); Chlorocebus, spp. (African green monkeys, vervets); Aotus, spp.; Papio, spp.; Callithrix, spp. (marmosets) Non-traditional animal models including but not limited to: Domestic livestock: horses, cattle, goats, sheep, fowl Wildlife species: marmots, wild rodents, deer, bats Invertebrates: snails, parasitic nematodes, parasitic protozoa, insect vectors of human disease Aquatic: zebrafish HFIM Pathogens: infectious bacteria, viruses, parasites, fungi, toxins, and other agents such as prions that cause clinical syndromes in humans (surrogate human pathog

description: Notice Type: Sources Sought Notice Number: PRARNG-27-SS39258 Notice Title: Sources Sought � Potential Sole-Source Construction-Phase (Title II / Type �C�) Architect-Engineer Services, Project No. 431850, Camp Santiago, Puerto Rico PSC: C219 � Architect and Engineering - General: Other NAICS Code: 541330 � Engineering Services (Size Standard: $25.5 Million) Publication Date: 20 November 2026 Response Date: 7 December 2026, 1600 AST Contracting Office: United States Property and Fiscal Office (USPFO) for Puerto Rico, Purchasing and Contracting Division, San Juan, PR 00904-9002 Synopsis: This is not a solicitation nor a request for Architect-Engineer Qualifications using SF 330. The Government will not issue an award resulting from this sources sought. There are no solicitation documents. This notice is for market-research purposes only. The United States Property and Fiscal Office (USPFO) for Puerto Rico is conducting market research to identify responsible sources capable of providing Construction-Phase Architect-Engineer services (commonly referred to within the National Guard as Title II / Type �C� services) for Project No. 431850, Engineering Housing Maintenance Shop (EHMS), Camp Santiago Joint Training Center, Salinas, Puerto Rico. The original Designer of Record, CH2M HILL�HDR JV (CAGE: 750V1), prepared and sealed the final design package (NGB Type A and Type B) under Task Order W912LR21F0002 and completed the Code and Criteria design recertification on 6 March 2026 under Contract W912LR25CA001. Construction Contract W912LR27CA001 was awarded on 16 October 2026. Notice to Proceed is anticipated on or about 8 December 2026, with initial technical submittals due on or about 7 January 2027 and physical construction mobilization scheduled for 30 January 2027. This requirement is for professional A-E services governed by 40 U.S.C. � 1101 et seq. and RFO FAR 36.102 and 36.202. The period of performance will be 730 calendar days. The selected firm must commence initial technical-submittal review services within five (5) calendar days after issuance of the A-E Notice to Proceed and provide construction-phase support no later than 15 January 2027. Required Construction-Phase (Title II / Type �C�) A-E services include registered professional engineering and architectural technical supervision, design-intent interpretations, technical evaluations and recommendations for Government approval on Requests for Information (RFIs), shop drawings, and technical submittals; on-site resident construction observation; inspection documentation and technical reporting in support of Government quality-assurance functions; review of material testing results; technical verification of red-line as-built record drawings; and design-conformance verification of building systems performance against the approved design baseline. All contractual direction that changes contract scope, price, terms, or schedule remains the exclusive authority of the Government Contracting Officer. The Construction-Phase A-E contractor will provide technical evaluations and recommendations only and will not direct the construction contractor or approve deviations from contract requirements. The Government is considering whether this requirement may qualify as a follow-on acquisition under 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1) and � 3204(b), as implemented by RFO FAR 6.103-1, on the basis of potential substantial duplication of cost or unacceptable delay. Information received in response to this notice will be evaluated and considered in determining whether to conduct a competitive A-E acquisition or pursue a sole-source approach. Key Considerations the Government Will Evaluate: The original firm�s continuing professional responsibility under its prior contracts and the requirements of Puerto Rico Law 173 of 1988 (20 L.P.R.A. �� 711 et seq.) regarding technical control and sealing of professional work. The effort and cost that would be required for a new firm to validate the existing final design record (207 drawing sheets, 2,217 specification pages, geotechnical report, and March 2026 recertification) and establish clear responsibility boundaries. Whether any firm can meet the required start dates (submittal review within five days of A-E NTP and on-site support by 15 January 2027) without causing delay to the construction contract. Response Instructions: This notice is issued for market-research purposes in accordance with RFO DFARS PGI 206.103-170(d) (AFARS 5106.103-170(d)) and RFO FAR 5.101. The Government is not requesting competitive request for qualifications or SF 330 submissions at this time. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The historical record file shall include,but not be limited to the following types of historical records: Receipt inspection documentation. Repair shop travelers or repair cards. Parts replacement records. Parts inspection data before and after repair as applicable. Acceptance test data. QA personn

title: C1AZ--631-21-011 Build Elevator Tower for Building 25 A/E Design SF330 Request for Qualifications
description: SPECIAL NOTICE FOR QUALIFICATIONS (SF 330) NAICS Code: 541330 Engineering Services (Small Business size standard $25.5M) A. INTRODUCTION: The VA Central Western Massachusetts Healthcare System (CWM HCS) plans to build and install a new elevator tower at Building 25 on the Leeds Campus. This project will correct a FCA deficiency. Provide all professional architectural and engineering (A/E) Part One Services (also known as Design Phase Type A & Type B Services) necessary to develop complete drawings, specifications, and cost estimates associated with building a new elevator tower at Building 25 and Part Two Services (also known as Construction Period Services Type C). The intent of this project includes but is not limited to: Evaluate existing elevator pit slab for buildings 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12, 16, 20, and 26 and design an elevator pit sump pump with oil interceptor. Design plumbing of oil water separator to sanitary sewer. See acceptable conceptual design attached. This conceptual design shall be validated. This shall be used to minimize and inform design efforts. Identify and address any issues or conflicts as necessary. If the elevator tower appearance is different than the conceptual design, conduct a Section 106 Historical Submission Report for VA to file with Massachusetts State Historical Preservation Office, by a Professional Historic Preservation Consultant. Existing report will be made available to the highest rated A/E firm. Conduct code compliance reviews (NFPA, ABAAS, VA Design Manuals, etc.) and integrate findings into design for compliance. Where conflicts exist between VA adopted codes and standards and the documents on the TIL, the A/E shall bring this to the attention of the VA. The resolution of the conflict shall be made by the authority having jurisdiction for VA to ensure consistency department wide. The A/E shall provide all services required to prepare documents and reports consistent with the VA s project team goals as prioritized during preliminary project meetings, field surveys and studies. The A/E shall determine existing conditions, severity of deficiencies, if any previous deficiencies have been corrected and to identify any conditions which may have previously been unreported. Cost estimates shall be prepared to reflect the cost of replacing the component in a standalone project (i.e., not as part of another project) and all costs including but not limited to asbestos removal if required, special field conditions and/or temporary equipment needed during the construction. Provide a Qualified Elevator Inspector during Construction Services to certify elevator. Also provide Part Two A/E Services (also known as Construction Period Services Type C) A/E Part Two Services of this design project (also known as Construction Period Services) includes responding to construction contractor Requests For Information (RFIs) during the solicitation (solicitation support) and construction phases of the construction project, attendance at post-award and commissioning kick off construction project conferences, review of construction material submittals and shop drawings, attendance at weekly teleconference construction meetings, approximately 1 site visits per month during active construction (both scheduled and emergent) to ensure compliance with the design drawings and specifications, preparation of site visit reports, coordination with project commissioning requirements/QEI inspection, review of any construction project modifications for cost and technical acceptability, attendance and participation during the pre-final inspection and final acceptance inspection, preparation of the punch list and preparation of record drawings of the completed construction project based on the construction contractor s as-built drawings. The A/E shall prepare a submittal log to be utilized by the VA during construction period services and maintain a RFI log. B. CONTRACT INFORMATION: The VA Medical Center Central Western Massachusetts located in Leeds, MA has a requirement for a Firm Fixed Price contract to provide professional A/E services for the 631-21-011 Building 25 Elevator Design project. The magnitude of construction is between $2,000,000 and $5,000,000. title: Notice of Intent - Sole Source - University Corporation for Advanced Internet Development, dba Internet2
description: The National Science Foundation intends to award a sole-source contract to University Corporation for Advanced Internet Development, dba Internet2 for Internet2 Non-Connected Affiliate Membership. The contemplated contract action is expected to result in a contract valued at approximately $39,861.00 and is anticipated to have a period of performance from 01/01/2027-12/31/2027. This notice is published in accordance with RFO FAR 5.101. Basis for Other Than Full and Open Competition The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source pursuant to RFO FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source. The National Science Foundation has determined that Internet2 is the only source reasonably available capable of satisfying the Government's requirement because: Failure to renew Internet2 services would significantly impact NSF's ability to maintain connectivity with research and education networks that support critical agency programs and partnerships. Loss of access to Internet2 could disrupt data-sharing activities, research collaboration efforts, and network-dependent services relied upon by NSF staff, researchers, and external stakeholders. Transitioning to an alternative provider would require substantial planning, implementation, testing, and coordination efforts and could result in service interruptions, additional costs, and operational delays Renewing Internet2 support represents the most efficient, cost-effective, and lowest-risk approach to maintaining continuity of NSF's research network services. Continued use of Internet2 preserves established connectivity, operational stability, and interoperability with existing research and education partners while avoiding the technical and operational risks associated with migrating to a different solution. As a result, competition is lacking because no other known source can provide the required supplies or services within the Government's required timeframe and technical requirements. Interested Sources This notice is not a request for proposals. Nevertheless, any responsible source that believes it can satisfy the Government's requirement may submit a capability statement demonstrating its ability to meet all requirements identified in this notice. Capability statements must be submitted electronically to the Point of Contact identified above no later than 4:00 PM EST, Monday, December 7, 2026. Responses will be evaluated solely to determine whether a bona fide competitive source exists for this requirement. Additional Information Intended Awardee: University Corporation for Advanced Internet Development, dba Internet2 Anticipated Award Date: 01/01/2027 Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price Place of Performance: 401 Dulany St., Alexandria, VA 22314 The Government reserves the right not to compete this requirement if no responses are received that clearly demonstrate an ability to satisfy the Government's requirement.

title: Infrastructure Support services
description: Headquarters Air Mobility Command HQ AMC/A6 requires engineering support for Virtualization, Cloud Networks, Secure and Non-Secure Networking, Network transmission for both wired and wireless, Assured Command and Control (C2) voice/video/data systems, and Advance Mobile Technology. The engineering support provides end-to-end technology analysis, assessments, and reviews of all technical solutions, products, services, and capabilities to ensure all are consistent with Department of War (DoW) and USAF base area network architecture and standards. These projects provide direct support to the Services (Army, Air Force, etc.), Combatant Commands (CCMDs), Joint Staff as well as the DoW business and acquisition communities depending on network access. HQ AMC communications equipment and systems are in continual need of technology refresh and upgrades that encompass system components, software, Local Area Networks (LANs), Wireless LANs, Network Multiplexing, voice and supporting infrastructures.

title: UTILITY EXCAVATION AND REPAIR SERVICES IDIQ
description: Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory (Fermilab) is soliciting proposals for an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) type Master Subcontract for Utilities Excavation and Repair Services for Fermilab located in Batavia, IL. Fermi Forward Discovery Group (FFDG) seeks to find a qualified subcontractor to perform on-call, scheduled, and emergency excavation services and utility repairs, as described in Exhibit C, Statement of Work, and the requirements of each task order. Work will be performed across the Fermilab site, which covers approximately 6,800 acres in Kane and DuPage Counties and includes approximately 375 buildings and structures. The site contains a wide variety of soil types and terrain, such as clay soils, fill, and saturated soils, in settings that include developed areas, open prairie, woodlands, wetlands, and areas adjacent to ponds and waterways. Offerors should consider these conditions in their technical approach, equipment selection, and pricing. Fermilab operates 24 hours per day, 365 days per year, and the work must support uninterrupted laboratory operations. The Request for Proposal and all Exhibits are located at Sam.gov under Solicitation number 385439GMK. Questions Close on November 18, 2026 at 5:00 pm CST. title: Germany – Structural shell work – Helios Fachklinik Schleswig - Forensik Verg.-Nr. 101 Rohbau- & Spezialtiefbauarbeiten (BA 1.1 Haus 14)
description: Gesamtkonzept: Am Neufelder Weg 18 bis 20 in Schleswig befindet sich das Klinikgelände der Klinik für Forensische Psychiatrie. Die Klinik plant auf dem vorhandenen geschlossenen Klinikgelände u.a. den Neubau des Hauses 14. Das neue Haus 14 wird unmittelbar hinter dem Altbau entstehen. Für die Bauphase wird ein von der Klinik getrennter Baustellenbereich geschaffen. Übergangsweise wird für diese Baustelle eine eigene Zufahrt geschaffen. Der Altbau von Haus 14 wird nach Fertigstellung und Bezug des Neubaus abgerissen. Die Baustellenzufahrt wird zurückgebaut. Der Neubau von Haus 14 erfolgt als Massivbaukörper in konventioneller Bauweise. Der Neubau wird auf drei Geschossen insgesamt 60 Behandlungsplätze für Patient*innen des geschlossenen Maßregelvollzuges anbieten. Haus 14 ist grundstücksbedingt in einem u-förmigen Grundriss konzipiert. Der Neubau erfolgt die Fassadengestaltung mit sandfarbenen Verblendsteinen. Die Fenster sind in grau gehalten. Mengengerüst Gewerk Rohbau: (1) Gründung: a. Tiefgründung auf Pfählen - ca. 100 Stck. - in Verbindung mit einem Balkenrost. b. Stb. Sohle auf Balkenrost; Menge ca. 1410 m² (2) Außenwand: a. 20 cm KS-Mauerwerk; Menge ca. 1.450 m² b. 20 cm Stb. Wände; Menge ca. 410 m² c. Fassade aus Verblendmauerwerk d. Sockel ca. 220 m gesamt (3) Innenwände: a. 24 cm KS-Mauerwerk; Menge ca. 1.450 m² b. 17,5 cm KS-Mauerwerk; Menge ca. 2.000 m² c. 11,5 cm KS-Mauerwerk; Menge ca. 1.300 m² d. 24 cm Stb. Wände; Menge ca. 800 m² (4) Stahlbetondecken: a. Menge ca. 4.230 m² gesamt (5) Putzfläche a. Auf Mauerwerk ca. 11.500 m² gesamt b. Auf Beton ca. 2.200 m² gesamt

title: Bulgaria – Repair and maintenance services of electrical machinery, apparatus and associated equipment – „Техническо обслужване и ремонт на дизелови генератори“
description: Изпълнението на дейностите по поддръжка и ремонт изисква посещения и работа в обекти, свързани с отбраната и сигурността на Република България, с ниво на достъп до класифицирана информация „Секретно“, което налага поставянето на изисквания към кандидатите да притежават Удостоверение за сигурност на юридическото лице и Разрешение за достъп до класифицирана информация на физическите лица, съгласно на ЗЗКИ, с минимално ниво на достъп до класифицирана информация „Секретно“ или по-високо. Техническото обслужване включва профилактични прегледи на всеки 6 (шест) месеца и профилактика със смяна на консумативи (един път годишно) на 25 броя дизелови генератори, монтирани в обекти на Изпълнителна агенция „Инфраструктура на електронното управление“. Услугите по извършване на ремонт се осигуряват при необходимост.

title: Bulgaria – Pipes and fittings – Изработка и доставка на линзови компенсатори по системa 5,6VC
description: Изработка и доставка на общо 48 броя линзови компенсатори по системa 5,6V, необходими за осигуряване на надеждната работа на тръбопроводите за всички експлоатационни режими и безопасна и дългосрочна експлоатация на 5 и 6 ЕБ. Техническите характеристики, количествата, условията и обемът, необходими за изпълнение на обществената поръчка, са подробно описани в Техническо задание № 24.ЕП-2.ТЗ.1467.

title: Bulgaria – Repair and maintenance services of electrical building installations – „Извършване на последваща проверка на електромери, собственост на „Електроразпределителни мрежи запад“ ЕАД“, реф. № РРS 26-118
description: „Електроразпределителни мрежи Запад“ ЕАД провежда процедура от вида „договаряне с предварителна покана за участие“ с предмет: „Извършване на последваща проверка на електромери, собственост на „Електроразпределителни мрежи запад“ ЕАД“, реф. № РРS 26-118. Предметът на обществената поръчка е разделен на пет обособени позиции, както следва: Обособена позиция 1 – Извършване на последваща проверка на електромери, собственост на „Електроразпределителни мрежи Запад“ ЕАД, за оперативни центрове: София Изток 1, София Изток 2, Левски, Плевен извънградски, Видин-Белоградчик; Обособена позиция 2 – Извършване на последваща проверка на електромери, собственост на „Електроразпределителни мрежи Запад“ ЕАД, за оперативни центрове: София Север 1, София Север 2, Червен бряг, Бяла Слатина-Козлодуй, Ловеч, Троян-Тетевен, Перник-Брезник, Радомир; Обособена позиция 3 – Извършване на последваща проверка на електромери, собственост на „Електроразпределителни мрежи Запад“ ЕАД, за оперативни центрове: София Запад 1, София Запад 2, Монтана, Лом, Дупница, Кюстендил, сектор Параметризация, сектор СТИ; Обособена позиция 4 – Извършване на последваща проверка на електромери, собственост на „Електроразпределителни мрежи Запад“ ЕАД, за оперативни центрове: Враца, Мездра, Ботевград, Самоков-Костенец, Пирдоп, Сливница-Своге, Благоевград, Сандански-Петрич, Разлог, Гоце Делчев; Обособена позиция 5 – Извършване на последваща проверка на електромери, собственост на „Електроразпределителни мрежи Запад“ ЕАД, за оперативни центрове: София Юг 1, София Юг 2, Плевен град-Гулянци. Всеки кандидат/участник може да участва само за една обособена позиция при условие, че отговаря на изискванията на Закона за обществените поръчки (ЗОП), Правилника за прилагане на ЗОП (ППЗОП) и на изискванията на Възложителя, включително на критериите за подбор, посочени в обявлението и документацията за обществената поръчка. Критерият за възлагане на настоящата обществена поръчка при определяне на икономически най-изгодната оферта е „най-ниска цена”, определена съгласно методиката за оценка на офертите от документацията.

title: SOLICITATION NOTICE- Massena NY Virtual Law Enforcement Training Facility- Construction
description: The purpose of Amendment #1 for the Massena Virtual Law Enforcement Training Facility- Construction solicitation is to extend the proposal due date from Saturday, November 21st, 2026 to Monday, December 7th, 2026 by 5:00pm EST and to include the attachment, "Site Visit Sign-In Sheet Massena Virtual Law Enforcement Training Facility." All proposals should be sent electronically via email to kyle.cole@gsa.gov. All other terms and conditions remain the same. A forthcoming amendment will include responses to all RFIs received before the RFI deadline. ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ Solicitation: Construction Services Contract for Massena Virtual Law Enforcement Training Facility- Construction project at the Massena LPOE, Rooseveltown, NY. Proposals are due Saturday, November 21st, 2026 by 5:00 pm EST. All proposals should be sent electronically via email to kyle.cole@gsa.gov. The on-site visit will be held on Thursday, October 15th at 10am EST. All individuals who would like to attend must email kyle.cole@gsa.gov at least one day prior to the site visit to confirm their attendance. The site visit is not mandatory, but is encouraged. Questions are due via email to kyle.cole@gsa.gov by close of business on Friday, October 30th, 2026. In order to receive the Specifications and Drawings for this solicitation, you must complete Attachment 10, "Safeguarding and Dissemination of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Building Information." The completed CUI Form must be sent via email to kyle.cole@gsa.gov. Reference is made to the PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE Notice ID EQPXCAC-26-0011. All solicitation posts and updates for the Massena Virtual Law Enforcement Training Facility- Construction project will be posted to Solicitation No. 47PC5326R0029. Massena Virtual Law Enforcement Training Facility- Construction project at the Massena LPOE, Rooseveltown, NY includes, but is not limited to providing all labor, materials, tools, management, and full time on-site supervision required by contract documents to construct a Virtual Law Enforcement Training Facility. The contract work incorporates site demolition/excavation/grading/planting/paving, general construction, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, hard-wall partitions, security, and telecommunication work to meet United States Customs and Border Protection (CBP) requirements as follows: 1) Selective demolition of Architectural, Mechanical and Electrical systems, construction, and finishes at nearby Building G to support the renovation work. 2) Mechanical, plumbing, electrical, communication, security, and fire suppression systems to serve the uses of the new facility. 3) Earthwork, exterior improvements, and utilities for new facility. 4) Installation of common floor, wall, and ceiling finishes. 5) Installation of specialty floor, wall, and ceiling finishes as required. The contractor shall expect to interface with the GSA Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) for all major Life Safety contract submittal reviews and approvals. Typically, all submittals, once completed, will be grouped and transmitted to the AHJ for review and final approval. The contractor shall expect to interface with the US Customs and Border Protection agency representatives at the Land Port of Entry for all major submittal reviews and approvals as well as coordination for the installation of supporting equipment and devices with the facility. Exact work description will be identified and indicated in the Contract Documents. Products to be used will be specified within the drawings and individual Specification Sections. The contractor shall comply with the projects design specifications and drawings. The work will be constructed under a single prime contractor who is to adhere to all security requirements and guidelines for building access. The awardee will be required to complete the security clearance process. The procurement will be solicited and awarded to one (1) Total Small Business set-aside contractor. Offers from other than small business concerns will not be considered by the agency. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code associated with this procurement is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The Small Business Administration standard of 45 million dollars in annual receipts averaged over the last three (3) completed fiscal years. This project shall be performed by an experienced Contractor that has performed similar work. The estimated performance period is 340 calendar days after Notice to Proceed has been issued. The magnitude of construction for this project is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. The procurement method that will be implemented for this project will be in accordance with FAR Part 15.1-Source Selection Processes and Techniques. This project is a competitive acquisition utilizing the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) selection process. The government will evaluate technical responses using three evaluation factors to determine the proposal that best meets the requirements of the government. The vendor's experience, past performance, and staffing plan are acceptable/unacceptable factors. If a vendor does not meet the criteria for the prior experience factor, or the past performance, and receive an unacceptable, it will receive no further consideration under this acquisition. The vendor�s prior experience, past performance and staffing plan/structural organization factors, are equal in importance. All the technical evaluation factors, when combined, are significantly more important than price. This Contract will be awarded to a vendor whose proposal provides the lowest price with technically acceptable criteria to meet the government�s needs. The planned project delivery method will result in a Firm-Fixed-Price contract for construction services. Performance and payment bonds will be required following award pursuant to the Miller Act. A bid guarantee is also required. A description of GSA�s policies and procedures, in addition to that outlined in FAR 43.204, that apply to definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts can be found at GSAM 552.243-71 Equitable Adjustments, https://www.acquisition.gov/gsam/552.243-71. Interested firms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM), in order to receive a contract award. Firms can register via the Internet site at https://www.sam.gov or by contacting SAM Service Desk at https://www.fsd.gov. The solicitation and associated information will only be available from the https://sam.gov website mentioned above. No telephone requests will be accepted. The solicitation will not be a sealed bid and there will not be a formal bid opening. All inquiries must be in writing, via email to the person(s) specified in the solicitation. All answers will be provided in writing and will be available on the aforementioned https://sam.gov posting. Offeror's will not be reimbursed for proposal submittal expenses. Several solicitation documents will be posted as "Locked" packages in the https://sam.gov posting. In order to view or download the packages, vendors must have a secure account. Information on how to register for an account and log in is available on the https://sam.gov website, under the "Getting Started" tab. Interested parties are strongly encouraged to register to this notice to receive notification of actions including posting of any amendments. However, offerors are advised to check the site frequently as they are responsible for obtaining amendments. DISCLAIMER: The official solicitation package and technical specifications will be located on the official Government web page and the Government is not liable for information furnished by any other source. Amendments, if/when issued, will be posted to the https://sam.gov website for electronic downloading. This will normally be the only method of distributing

title: Lease of Office Space within Philadelphia, PA. Request for Lease Proposals (RLP) #26NAT02
description: This advertisement is incorporated by reference into Request for Lease Proposals (RLP) #26NAT02 as an attachment. HOW TO OFFER The Leasing Portal (https://leasing.gsa.gov) enables interested parties to offer space to the Federal Government through a secure, web-based process. To participate, register on the site by selecting �Register to Offer Space� and follow the instructions provided. Helpful resources�including instructional guides and video tutorials�are available on the portal under the Resources tab. The Open Period runs from the 1st through the 7th of each month, ending at 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time unless otherwise stated by the Government and unless the 7th falls on a weekend or Federal Holiday. If the 7th falls on a weekend or Federal Holiday, the Open Period will end at 8:00 PM (ET) on the next business day. No submissions are accepted during the Closed Period. During an Open Period, users may submit new offers, or modify or withdraw existing ones. Lease awards will be made to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable offer without negotiations. Offered space must comply with all applicable Federal, State, and Local jurisdiction requirements, including standards for fire and life safety, accessibility, seismic resilience, and energy efficiency. IMPORTANT NOTES Check the attachments and links section of this notice for possible, additional project-specific requirements or modifications to the RLP. SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Kennedy Space Center (KSC) is hereby soliciting information from potential sources capable of maintaining and operating NASA facilities, systems, equipment, and utilities (FSEU) at KSC and Cape Canaveral Space Force Station (CCSFS); and providing logistics and other technical support services at KSC under a fixed price contract. The Spaceport Infrastructure, Maintenance, and Operations (SIMO) contract will succeed KSC�s Base Operations and Spaceport Services (BOSS) contract; however, complete requirements under the performance work statement are to be defined. Requirements contemplated under this acquisition reflect a significant departure from the services under the BOSS contract and its canceled follow-on procurement for Spaceport Operations and Center Services. Specifically, NASA is assuming end-to-end engineering responsibility for all assigned FSEU. Additionally, NASA will perform engineering analysis, causal determination, technical disposition, system-level evaluation, and corrective-action development. NASA will also directly operate and manage continuous spaceport integration activities including real-time monitoring, conflict assessment, and customer communication for all KSC Spaceport operations. This includes providing scheduling and master schedule management, integrated outage coordination and infrastructure impact management, prescribed burn coordination, and transport integration and hardware movement oversight. Finally, NASA will perform construction support services to include participation in workforce planning for Construction of Facility (CoF) and Local Authority projects; providing recommendations on necessary construction support levels; attending design reviews; reviewing design packages for constructability; participating in construction status discussions; and providing coordination and project-administration support. The SIMO contract is expected to support over 30 customers, including NASA, other Government agencies, and commercial customers, across approximately 220 square miles, primarily at KSC, Florida, and CCSFS, Florida. Performance under the contract is anticipated to commence no earlier than April 2027. title: Post Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Readiness and Validation Status
description: https://feedback.gsa.gov/jfe/form/SV_3t6dNlgkS4Vg6iy Federal agencies are preparing for the transition from cryptographic algorithms that may be vulnerable to future quantum computing attacks to quantum-resistant cryptographic algorithms standardized by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Public key cryptographic algorithms (i.e. asymmetric cryptography) currently used across Federal information systems, products and services � including Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA), elliptic curve Diffie-Hellman(ECDH), elliptic curve digital signature algorithms (ECDSA), and related mechanisms � will be vulnerable to a future cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer (CRQC). As a result, Federal agencies are expected to identify, prioritize, and migrate quantum-vulnerable cryptographic systems to approved post-quantum cryptographic algorithms. Federal agencies are also required to use validated cryptographic algorithms and modules when cryptography is required to protect Federal information or Federal systems. The NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program establishes requirements under FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3. FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3 requirements are applicable to U.S. Federal agencies when cryptographic-based security systems are used to provide information security for Federal operations and assets. If cryptography is required for the protection of information or data, then FIPS-validated cryptography is applicable. Non-validated cryptography shall be treated as providing no validated protection for Federal information where validated cryptography is required. Relevant policy, standards, and guidance include, but may not be limited to: NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program; FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules; FIPS 203, Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard; FIPS 204, Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard; FIPS 205, Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard; NIST SP 800-208, Recommendation for Stateful Hash-Based Signature Schemes; NIST SP 800-52, Guidelines for the Selection, Configuration, and Use of Transport Layer Security Implementations; OMB Memorandum M-22-09, Moving the U.S. Government Toward Zero Trust Cybersecurity Principles; Executive Order 14306, Sustaining Select Efforts to Strengthen the Nation�s Cybersecurity; Executive Order 14412, Securing the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks; OMB Memorandum M-26-15, Execution of the Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography; and CISA guidance regarding product categories and technologies that use post-quantum cryptography standards. This RFI is intended to collect industry information regarding the availability, validation status, product and service readiness, procurement accessibility, implementation maturity, operational impacts, interoperability, and migration support associated with commercial products and services that support, or plan to support, NIST-approved post-quantum cryptography standards. This Request for Information is issued for market research purposes only. There are no anticipated tasks under this RFI. This RFI is intended to collect information from industry regarding vendor capabilities, products and services availability, cryptographic validation status, contract accessibility, and readiness to support the Federal Government�s migration to post-quantum cryptography (PQC). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation, Request for Proposal, Request for Quotation, Invitation for Bid, or promise to issue a future solicitation. Any contract or order that may result from information received through this RFI will be subject to applicable procurement laws, regulations, and competition requirements. The Government is not responsible for any costs incurred by industry in preparing or submitting responses to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI are solely at the respondent�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future solicitation, if one is issued. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned.

title: RFI: Industry Interest in Use of NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) Test Facilities and Capabilities
description: Public Notice/Announcement � Request for Information (RFI) THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. NO PROPOSALS ARE TO BE SUBMITTED IN RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Office of JPL Management and Oversight (NOJMO) to solicit responses from all interested parties. This document is for information and planning purposes and to allow industry the opportunity to express interest in the use of NASA�s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) test facilities. This RFI is a standalone market research effort and is not related to, a continuation of, or a supplement to any previous RFI issued by NASA or NOJMO concerning the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), its facilities, capabilities, or potential industry use. This RFI is not related to any current or future competitive acquisition for the operation of the JPL. Responses to any prior RFI should not be considered responsive to this notice, and information submitted in response to a previous RFI does not constitute a response to this RFI. This notice is issued for informational and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposals, or an offer or commitment by the Government to enter into a contract or other type of agreement. Purpose The Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), a federally funded research and development center operated by the California Institute of Technology for NASA, maintains a broad portfolio of world-class facilities and test capabilities supporting spacecraft, instruments, robotics, and advanced technology development. NASA is conducting market research to assess industry interest in the potential short-term or medium-term utilization of select JPL facilities and capabilities. The purpose of this RFI is to: Understand potential demand for JPL test and integration facilities and services located in La Ca�ada Flintridge, California and other NASA-owned facilities managed or operated under JPL purview Inform internal planning related to facility utilization and potential access models Identify general categories of industry use cases and constraints Assess potential workforce, scheduling, and infrastructure considerations associated with external facility use In addition to facilities located at the primary JPL campus, certain capabilities may exist at associated NASA sites managed by JPL, including the Table Mountain Facility in Wrightwood, California, which supports optical communications, astronomy, and related technology demonstrations. Representative Facility Capabilities (see Attachment A) Representative Support Services (see Attachment A) Cost Recovery and Facility Use Considerations External use of NASA facilities is generally subject to cost recovery and usage fees consistent with federal policy governing the use of government-owned facilities and infrastructure. Depending on the nature of the activity, facility use may require reimbursement to NASA for costs including: facility operations and maintenance technical support services utilities and infrastructure usage scheduling and administrative support Specific cost structures or pricing models are not defined at this stage and may vary depending on the scope and duration of any future activities. Workforce and Staffing Considerations NASA is interested in understanding how potential industry users would envision staffing activities conducted within JPL facilities. Respondents are encouraged to address: Whether they anticipate bringing their own technical personnel to conduct testing or development activities within the facilities. The extent to which they may wish to leverage existing JPL or Caltech technical staff, engineering expertise, or operational support already available onsite. Any considerations related to workforce integration, safety training, or operational oversight. This information will help NASA understand potential operational models for facility utilization. Requested Industry Input Interested parties are invited to provide non-binding input addressing: General interest in utilizing the aforementioned test facilities. Types of activities or use cases that may benefit from access and utilization of such facilities. Anticipated duration (short-term or medium-term). High-level scheduling, access, or integration considerations. Whether respondents anticipate bringing their own personnel or utilizing JPL technical staff. The type of agreement or legal instrument the respondent believes would be most appropriate for the proposed and the basis for that preference. Any facility or infrastructure requirements not listed above. Response Instructions NASA invites responses from all categories of U.S. domestic entities, including commercial firms, academic institutions, and federal and state organizations, as well as United States Commercial Providers as defined in the Space Commerce Act, 51 U.S.C. � 50101(7). Responses are limited to U.S. entities only. Interested parties should submit responses electronically in MS word or PDF format. Responses should not exceed 30 pages and should directly address the items identified under "Requested Industry Input" above. Responses shall be submitted via NASA�s Enterprise File Sharing and Sync Box (EFSS Box), a FedRAMP Moderate certified platform. Electronic submissions shall not contain hidden formulas, tables, be locked, be password protected, or contain links to data not included in the electronic copy. All electronic submissions should be searchable and should not contain scanned documents, except those documents that must be provided in their native format (e.g., signature pages). Interested parties shall ensure documents are free from viruses and malware, as documents determined by NASA to contain a virus or malware will not be opened or reviewed. Responses must be submitted to: https://nasagov.app.box.com/f/a2d4260d157d416882015f7432bf5486. Interested parties shall follow instructions regarding capability statement submission found at: https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/other/EFSS-Box-Offeror-Proposal-Submission-Instructions.pdf This RFI may be amended or withdrawn by NASA at any time. NASA seeks to ensure broad awareness and visibility of this notice; however, it is each respondent's responsibility to monitor SAM.gov for any amendments or additional information related to this notice. Responses are voluntary and will be used solely for market research purposes and will not affect the ability to propose on future opportunities. NASA does not intend to award a contract, Space Act Agreement (SAA), or any other legal implementing instrument in response to submissions received from this RFI. NASA will not pay for any information submitted in response to this RFI, nor will NASA reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing a response. This notice does not imply facility availability, partnership, or future acquisition. All submissions become the property of the Government and will not be returned. It is not NASA's intent to publicly disclose responses or proprietary information submitted in response to this RFI. Still, Respondents should clearly mark any proprietary or confidential information. No, Personally Identifiable Information (PII) should be submitted in response to this RFI. NASA will protect such information from public disclosure to the extent permitted by the Freedom of Information Act and other applicable laws and regulations. NASA does not intend to reply individually to respondents but reserves the right to contact respondents for clarification or to conduct follow-up discussions, if needed. Based on the responses received through this market research, NASA may consider hosting a future Industry Day or similar engagement opportunity to provide additional information regarding available test facilities, potential access models, and the technical expertise of the workforce at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory. SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Kennedy Space Center (KSC) is hereby soliciting information from potential sources capable of maintaining and operating NASA facilities, systems, equipment, and utilities (FSEU) at KSC and Cape Canaveral Space Force Station (CCSFS); and providing logistics and other technical support services at KSC under a fixed price contract. The Spaceport Infrastructure, Maintenance, and Operations (SIMO) contract will succeed KSC�s Base Operations and Spaceport Services (BOSS) contract; however, complete requirements under the performance work statement are to be defined. Requirements contemplated under this acquisition reflect a significant departure from the services under the BOSS contract and its canceled follow-on procurement for Spaceport Operations and Center Services. Specifically, NASA is assuming end-to-end engineering responsibility for all assigned FSEU. Additionally, NASA will perform engineering analysis, causal determination, technical disposition, system-level evaluation, and corrective-action development. NASA will also directly operate and manage continuous spaceport integration activities including real-time monitoring, conflict assessment, and customer communication for all KSC Spaceport operations. This includes providing scheduling and master schedule management, integrated outage coordination and infrastructure impact management, prescribed burn coordination, and transport integration and hardware movement oversight. Finally, NASA will perform construction support services to include participation in workforce planning for Construction of Facility (CoF) and Local Authority projects; providing recommendations on necessary construction support levels; attending design reviews; reviewing design packages for constructability; participating in construction status discussions; and providing coordination and project-administration support. The SIMO contract is expected to support over 30 customers, including NASA, other Government agencies, and commercial customers, across approximately 220 square miles, primarily at KSC, Florida, and CCSFS, Florida. Performance under the contract is anticipated to commence no earlier than April 2027. NASA is seeking capability statements from all interested parties, including all socioeconomic categories of small businesses and Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU)/Minority Institutions (MI) for the purposes of determining the appropriate level of competition and/or small business subcontracting goals. Vendors are encouraged to demonstrate capabilities as a prime, subcontractor and/or teaming partner. The Government reserves the right to consider a small business, small disadvantaged business (SDB), historically underutilized business zone, veteran owned small business, service-disabled veteran owned small business, or women-owned small business set-aside based on responses received. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 561210, All Other Support Services, and the corresponding small business size standard is $47 million. SECTION 2: SERVICES/SCOPE Preventative maintenance includes performing preventive maintenance (PM) and predictive testing and inspection (PTI) on assigned FSEU in approximately 900 facilities of varying complexity. Assigned FSEU includes, but is not limited to, high voltage/medium voltage power; low voltage power; electronic security systems; traffic signaling systems; oxygen deficiency monitoring systems; fire alarm systems; fire suppression systems; Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) and compressed air systems; elevators and chairlifts; plumbing; water distribution; wastewater collection a

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Kennedy Space Center (KSC) is hereby soliciting information from potential sources capable of maintaining and operating NASA facilities, systems, equipment, and utilities (FSEU) at KSC and Cape Canaveral Space Force Station (CCSFS); and providing logistics and other technical support services at KSC under a fixed price contract. The Spaceport Infrastructure, Maintenance, and Operations (SIMO) contract will succeed KSC�s Base Operations and Spaceport Services (BOSS) contract; however, complete requirements under the performance work statement are to be defined. Requirements contemplated under this acquisition reflect a significant departure from the services under the BOSS contract and its canceled follow-on procurement for Spaceport Operations and Center Services. Specifically, NASA is assuming end-to-end engineering responsibility for all assigned FSEU. Additionally, NASA will perform engineering analysis, causal determination, technical disposition, system-level evaluation, and corrective-action development. NASA will also directly operate and manage continuous spaceport integration activities including real-time monitoring, conflict assessment, and customer communication for all KSC Spaceport operations. This includes providing scheduling and master schedule management, integrated outage coordination and infrastructure impact management, prescribed burn coordination, and transport integration and hardware movement oversight. Finally, NASA will perform construction support services to include participation in workforce planning for Construction of Facility (CoF) and Local Authority projects; providing recommendations on necessary construction support levels; attending design reviews; reviewing design packages for constructability; participating in construction status discussions; and providing coordination and project-administration support. The SIMO contract is expected to support over 30 customers, including NASA, other Government agencies, and commercial customers, across approximately 220 square miles, primarily at KSC, Florida, and CCSFS, Florida. Performance under the contract is anticipated to commence no earlier than April 2027. NASA is seeking capability statements from all interested parties, including all socioeconomic categories of small businesses and Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU)/Minority Institutions (MI) for the purposes of determining the appropriate level of competition and/or small business subcontracting goals. Vendors are encouraged to demonstrate capabilities as a prime, subcontractor and/or teaming partner. The Government reserves the right to consider a small business, small disadvantaged business (SDB), historically underutilized business zone, veteran owned small business, service-disabled veteran owned small business, or women-owned small business set-aside based on responses received. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 561210, All Other Support Services, and the corresponding small business size standard is $47 million. title: Umbau, Sanierung und Erweiterung Grundschule am Harrl - Trockenbauabbruch Phase 4
description: Das Schulgebäude ist ein ca. 1876 erbauter historischer Massivbau, unterkellert und 4- geschossig. Das Schulgebäude ist als Baudenkmal nach § 3 Abs. 2 NDSchG eingestuft. Das Hauptgebäude enthält die Unterrichts-, Gruppen- und Differenzierungsräume, die Verwaltung, Mehrzweckräume sowie Nebenräume. Im UG befindet sich neben Lager- und Technikräumen ein Werkraum sowie eine Lehrküche, diese Nutzungen sollen im Zuge des Umbaus ertüchtigt werden. In der Phase 1 wurde ein drittes Treppenhaus über alle Geschosse und ein Mensaneubau (mit Musikräumen im 2.OG) errichtet. In der Phase 2 wurde das 3.OG (ehemalige Hausmeisterwohnung und der nicht genutzte Dachboden) zu Schulräumen umgenutzt und eine Lüftungsanlage im Dachboden eingebaut. Die Sanierung der Sanitärkerne mit Erstellung von neuen Steigesträngen erfolgte ebenfalls in Phase 2. Die Sanitärkerne und das 2.OG (Phase 3) sind derzeit noch Baustellenbereich. Ursprünglich sollte das Schulgebäude im laufenden Betrieb in den nächsten Jahren abschnittsweise saniert, umgebaut und erweitert werden. Damit die restlichen Geschosse unabhängig vom Schulbetrieb fertiggestellt werden können, wird der komplette Schulbetrieb ausgelagert. Voraussichtlich kann nach den Herbstferien 2026 die restliche Sanierung starten. In diesem Bauabschnitt (Phase 4) soll das 1. OG/ EG und der Rest des Kellergeschosses in einem Zuge saniert werden. Der Fußbodenaufbau im 2.OG ist ebenfalls zu entfernen Hinweis: Bei allen Abbrucharbeiten sind Feuerlöscher in unmittelbarer Nähe bereitzuhalten.

title: Udbud af rammeaftale vedr. rekrutteringsydelser til top- og lederstillinger på Københavns Universitet
description: Københavns Universitetet (Universitetet) har løbende behov for ekstern bistand til search og rekruttering i forbindelse med rekruttering af ledere og lignende medarbejdere. Universitetet er en stor og kompleks vidensorganisation med forskning, uddannelse og administration, høj faglig autonomi, international orientering og mange forskellige ledelsesopgaver. Derfor udbyder Universitetet nærværende rammeaftale vedrørende rekrutteringsydelser til top- og lederstillinger (”Rammeaftalen”). For en nærmere beskrivelse af Rammeaftalen og den udbudte opgave henviser Universitetet til det samlede udbudsmateriale angivet i afsnit 2 i udbudsbetingelserne. Universitetet har valgt at udbyde én samlet rammeaftale i stedet for at opdele aftalen i delaftaler, da det er Universitetets vurdering, at de efterspurgte rekrutteringsydelser indgår som led i en samlet og løbende understøttelse af Universitetets rekrutteringsbehov, at ydelserne er tæt forbundne i både indhold og gennemførelse, og at en opdeling i delydelser vil medføre øget administrativ belastning i form af flere kontraktforhold, større koordineringsbehov og mere ressourcekrævende opfølgning. Rammeaftalens anslåede værdi er DKK 10 mio., ekskl. moms, mens Rammeaftalens maksimale værdi er DKK 15 mio., ekskl. moms. Rammeaftalen træder i kraft ved begge parters underskrift og løber i to år fra ikrafttrædelsen. Universitetet kan ved skriftlig meddelelse forlænge aftalen med op til yderligere to år på uændret vilkår.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Rahmenvereinbarung "Systemische Beratung zu Qualitätsinfrastruktur"
description: Die Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB) unterstützt im Rahmen ihrer Entwicklungszusammenarbeit Partnerländer beim systemischen Auf- und Ausbau ihrer Qualitätsinfrastruktur (siehe https://www.ptb.de/cms/ptb/fachabteilungen/abt9/gruppe-93.html). Eine besondere Bedeutung kommt hierbei der strategischen Beratung zu Qualitätsinfrastruktur für nachhaltige Wirtschaftsentwicklung, Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und Handel sowie Umwelt und Klimaschutz zu. Der regionale Schwerpunkt liegt aktuell in Osteuropa, Zentralasien, Lateinamerika sowie Südostasien. Für die systemische Beratung von Institutionen der Qualitätsinfrastruktur in der Entwicklungszusammenarbeit sollen im Leistungszeitraum vom 15.02.2027 bis 14.02.2029 von einem Berater/ einer Beraterin u.A. folgende Aufgaben übernommen werden: ·Strategische und systemische Beratung zu Qualitätsinfrastruktur sowie überregionale Vernetzung, nach Absprache und Spezifikation mit den jeweiligen Partnerorganisationen und der PTB, ·Unterstützung der PTB bei der Leistungserbringung (Ad hoc Beratung, Umfeldbeobachtung) gegenüber dem Ministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ), insbesondere hinsichtlich der Handlungsfelder Internationaler Handel und Entwicklung der Qualitätsinfrastruktur und weitere siehe Leistungsbeschreibung.

title: Germany – Health and safety services – Ersatzneubau Neue Gertraudenbrücke - Leistungen zu Sicherheit und Gesundheitsschutz auf Baustellen
description: Aufgrund des geschädigten Bauwerkszustandes der Neuen Gertraudenbrücke wird ein Ersatzneubau vorgesehen. In diesem Zusammenhang werden die beidseitig verlaufenden Uferwege auf das neue Brückenniveau angehoben. Hierfür ist der Neubau der beidseitigen Uferwände erforderlich. Weiterhin wird eine Freianlagengestaltung für das umliegende Gelände vorgenommen und eine Grundinstandsetzung der parallel befindlichen (historischen) Gertraudenbrücke vorgesehen. Auftragsgegenstand sind Leistungen des Sicherheits- und Gesundheitsschutzkoordinators in der Bauausführung von Ingenieurbauwerken und der Verkehrsanlage. Hierzu gehören Leistungen während der Bauausführung, u.a. Einsatz als SiGeKo auf der Baustelle inkl. Sicherheitsbegehungen und -besprechungen, Durchführung von Arbeiten nach § 3 BaustellV, Erstellung und Fortschreibung von Unterlagen (Vorankündigung, SiGe-Plan, Arbeits- und Sicherheitsplan).

description: Verhandlungsverfahren mit Teilnahmewettbewerb entsprechend § 12 KonzVgV i.V.m. § 14 Abs. 2, Abs. 3 Nr. 2, Nr. 3 VgV, § 119 Abs. 5 GWB (zweistufiges Verhandlungsverfahren) zur Bestimmung eines Netzbetreibers für die Planung, die Errichtung und den Betrieb eines Gigabit-Netzes im Wirtschaftlichkeitslückenmodell in den ausgeschriebenen Ausbaugebieten nach Maßgabe der Richtlinie "Förderung zur Unterstützung des Gigabitausbau der Telekommunikationsnetze in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland" vom 31.03.2023 in der Fassung der 2. Änderung vom 13.01.2025 (nachfolgend "Gigabit-RL 2.0"). Wesentliche Grundlage des Verfahrens sind die "Rahmenregelung der Bundesrepublik Deutschland zur Unterstützung des flächendeckenden Aufbaus von Gigabitnetzen" vom 01.08.2024 (nachfolgend "Gigabit-RR 2.0"), die Richtlinie "Förderung zur Unterstützung des Gigabitausbaus der Telekommunikationsnetze in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland" vom 31.03.2023 in der Fassung der 2. Änderung vom 13.01.2025 (nachfolgend Gigabit-RL 2.0) sowie die Mitteilung der Europäischen Union "Leitlinien für staatliche Beihilfen zur Förderung von Breitbandnetzen" vom 31.01.2023 (2023/C 36/01). Die ausgeschriebenen Adressen des Erschließungsgebietes sind nach Ergebnis der Markterkundung förderfähige unterversorgte Adressen im Sinne der Gigabit-RL 2.0. Aus diesem Grund soll dort auf Basis dieses Auswahlverfahrens ein Gigabit-Netz als technologieneutrale Netzbezeichnung (Netz mit einer Breitbandversorgung von mindestens 1 Gbit/s symmetrisch zu Spitzenlastzeitbedingungen für alle Endnutzer der ausgeschriebenen Adressen) in den unterversorgten Gebieten errichtet werden, wobei sich die Up- und Downloadraten mindestens verdoppeln müssen. Auf die Vorgaben der "B-Leistungsbeschreibung" inkl. deren Anlagen wird ergänzend verwiesen. Der Konzessionsgeber ordnet den ausgeschriebenen "Vertrag über die Weiterleitung von Zuwendungen im Rahmen des Gigabitausbaus in der Gemeinde Bachhagel zum Zwecke der Planung, der Errichtung und des Betriebs eines gigabitfähigen Breitbandnetzes im Wirtschaftlichkeitslückenmodell nach der Richtlinie "Förderung zur Unterstützung des Gigabitausbaus der Telekommunikationsnetze in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland - Gigabit-Richtlinie des Bundes 2.0 (Gigabit-RL 2.0)" als eine Dienstleistungskonzession i.S.d. § 105 Abs. 1 Nr. 2 GWB ein. Der Konzessionsgeber überträgt damit die ihm als Aufgabe der Daseinsvorsorge obliegende Realisierung der Versorgung der Bevölkerung mit Gigabitanschlüssen auf den Konzessionsnehmer, welcher das Nutzungsrecht am Gigabit-Netz erhält und die Vergütung für seine Tätigkeit in erster Linie durch die Entgelte der Endkunden erhält, während der Konzessionsgeber lediglich einen Zuschuss zur Deckung der gegebenenfalls ausgewiesenen Wirtschaftlichkeitslücke leistet, welcher nach § 105 Abs. 1 Nr. 2 GWB einer Dienstleistungskonzession nicht entgegensteht. Der Schwerpunkt der Tätigkeit des Konzessionsnehmers liegt auf der Dienstleistung des Betreibens des Breitbandnetzes über den Zeitraum von mindestens sieben Jahren. Der Konzessionsgeber ordnet weiter das zu planende, zu bauende und zu betreibende Gigabit-Netz auch als ein "öffentliches Kommunikationsnetz" i.S.d. Bereichsausnahme gemäß § 149 Nr. 8 GWB ein, so dass der 4. Teil des GWB nicht zur Anwendung kommt. Soweit in den Unterlagen des Auswahlverfahrens auf Normen des 4. Teils des GWB verwiesen wird, begründet dies keinen Anspruch auf deren Anwendbarkeit.

buyer: Niedersächsisches Landesamt für Brand- und Katastrophenschutz
title: Germany – Construction work for buildings relating to law and order or emergency services and for military buildings – TNW: NLBK Neubau Unterkunftsgebäude, Celle-Scheuen
description: Das Niedersächsische Landesamt für Brand- und Katastrophenschutz plant die Entwicklung eines zusammenhängenden Unterkunftscampus auf dem Übungs- und Ausbildungsgelände für Brand- und Ka-tastrophenschutz am Standort Reiherberg 112 in Celle-Scheuen. Hierfür ist die Errichtung von zunächst zwei gleichartigen Gemeinschaftsunterkunftsgebäuden vorgesehen, mittelfristig soll der Campus auf insgesamt fünf Gebäude erweitert werden. Zu berücksichtigen sind zukünftige Entwicklungen wie die Möglichkeit einer baulichen Erweiterung als Campuslösung mit insgesamt fünf gleichartigen Unterkunftsgebäuden auf dem Grundstück. Die Umsetzung erfolgt auf einem im Eigentum des Landes Niedersachsen stehenden Grundstück und dient der langfristigen Sicherstellung sowie Erweiterung der Unterbringungskapazitäten am Standort.
